examples.f: ｜試験[しけん]の｜結果[けっか]が｜気[き]になってならない。

examples.ja: 彼の話は何かおかしいと思えてならない。
examples.en: I can't help feeling there's something off about his story.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]の｜話[はなし]は｜何[なに]かおかしいと｜思[おも]えてならない。

synonyms.note: てたまらない stresses a feeling almost too strong to bear; てならない stresses a feeling that arises on its own and won't stop.
てしょうがない is the more casual 'can't help ~'; てならない is somewhat more formal and literary.

entry.title: てこそ
entry.meaning: only by doing ~; it is precisely because one does ~
entry.summary: てこそ combines the て-form with the emphatic particle こそ to single out an action as the essential condition for a valued result — 努力してこそ成功する = 'it is only through effort that one succeeds'. The clause after it is normally positive and desirable: the point is that the good outcome is possible only because of the highlighted action.
pitfalls: The following clause is usually a positive or worthwhile result, since てこそ praises the condition that makes it possible.
It presents the action as the one indispensable condition; a plain から just gives a reason without that emphasis.

examples.ja: 困難を乗り越えてこそ、人は成長できる。
examples.en: It is precisely by overcoming hardships that people grow.
examples.f: ｜困難[こんなん]を｜乗り越[のりこ]えてこそ、｜人[ひと]は｜成長[せいちょう]できる。

examples.ja: 努力を続けてこそ、本当の実力が身につく。
examples.en: Only by keeping up the effort does one gain real ability.
examples.f: ｜努力[どりょく]を｜続[つづ]けてこそ、｜本当[ほんとう]の｜実力[じつりょく]が｜身[み]につく。

synonyms.note: て初めて means 'not until ~ did ...', stressing a first realization; てこそ stresses the essential condition for a good result.

related.note: こそ is the underlying emphatic particle ('precisely'); てこそ applies it to a verb as the key condition.
ばこそ ('precisely because') is a more formal, literary way to stress a reason; てこそ focuses on an enabling action.

entry.title: てからでないと
entry.meaning: not until you first do; can't unless you do first
entry.summary: 〜てからでないと sets a required first step — nothing further can happen until it's done. It's usually followed by a negative outcome: 予約してからでないと入れない = you can't get in unless you book first. Literally 'if it isn't after doing ~.'
structure: Verb［て form］＋ からでないと／からでなければ ＋ （negative）
pitfalls: The second clause is normally negative (〜ない／〜できない): 確認してからでないと答えられない.
It stresses order — X must come first before Y is possible; plain てから just says 'after,' without the 'can't otherwise' nuance.

examples.ja: 手を洗ってからでないと、食べてはいけません。
examples.en: You mustn't eat until you've washed your hands first.
examples.f: ｜手[て]を｜洗[あら]ってからでないと、｜食[た]べてはいけません。

examples.ja: 上司に確認してからでないと、返事ができません。
examples.en: I can't give an answer until I've checked with my boss first.
examples.f: ｜上司[じょうし]に｜確認[かくにん]してからでないと、｜返事[へんじ]ができません。

related.note: てから simply means 'after doing'; てからでないと adds that nothing else is possible until then.
なければならない states that an action is necessary; てからでないと makes that action a prerequisite for something else.

entry.title: 〜て以来
entry.meaning: ever since ~; since (a past event)
entry.summary: 以来 marks a point in the past after which a situation has continued unchanged up to now. It follows either the て-form of a verb (卒業して以来 = 'ever since graduating') or a noun (入社以来 = 'ever since joining the company'). The event is a single past change, and the clause that follows describes a state that has held ever since.
pitfalls: 以来 marks a one-time past event as a starting point; it does not work for repeated or ongoing actions.
The following clause describes a lasting state or tendency that continues to the present, not a single later event.
For close, recent time frames (yesterday, this morning) 以来 sounds odd; it implies a stretch of time has passed.

examples.ja: 大学を卒業して以来、彼とは一度も会っていない。
examples.en: I haven't seen him even once since I graduated from university.
examples.f: ｜大学[だいがく]を｜卒業[そつぎょう]して｜以来[いらい]、｜彼[かれ]とは｜一[いち]｜度[ど]も｜会[あ]っていない。

examples.ja: この製品は、発売以来ずっと人気が続いている。
examples.en: This product has stayed popular ever since it went on sale.
examples.f: この｜製品[せいひん]は、｜発売[はつばい]｜以来[いらい]ずっと｜人気[にんき]が｜続[つづ]いている。

synonyms.note: てから simply means 'after doing ~'; 以来 adds that the resulting state has lasted continuously up to now.

entry.title: に過ぎない
entry.meaning: no more than; merely; just
entry.summary: に過ぎない downplays something as being nothing more than what precedes it — ただの噂に過ぎない ('it's nothing but a rumor'). It minimizes the scale or importance of the thing, often to push back against an overestimation.
structure: Verb／い-adjective［plain form］＋ に過ぎない
pitfalls: It belittles or limits ('only that, nothing beyond'), and often pairs with ただ／ほんの ('mere') for emphasis.
With nouns, attach directly with no だ: 言い訳に過ぎない, not 言い訳だに過ぎない.

examples.ja: これはほんの一例に過ぎず、ほかにも多くの問題がある。
examples.en: This is merely one example; there are many other problems as well.
examples.f: これはほんの｜一[いち]｜例[れい]に｜過[す]ぎず、ほかにも｜多[おお]くの｜問題[もんだい]がある。

examples.ja: 彼はただ命令に従ったに過ぎないと主張した。
examples.en: He insisted that he had merely followed orders.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]はただ｜命令[めいれい]に｜従[したが]ったに｜過[す]ぎないと｜主張[しゅちょう]した。

synonyms.note: のみ is a formal 'only' limiting quantity; に過ぎない adds the judgment that it's unimportantly small.
だけ neutrally marks 'only'; に過ぎない spins that 'only' as a dismissive 'merely, nothing more'.

related.note: にほかならない emphatically insists something is precisely X; に過ぎない dismisses it as no more than X.

entry.title: に限る
entry.meaning: nothing beats ~; ~ is the best
entry.summary: に限る states the speaker's opinion that nothing is better than the thing named — 'you can't beat ~ / ~ is best'. It follows a noun or a plain verb: 疲れた時は寝るに限る ('when you're tired, nothing beats sleeping'), 夏はビールに限る ('in summer you can't beat a beer'). It is a warm, personal recommendation.
structure: Noun／Verb［dictionary form］／Verb［ない form］＋ に限る
pitfalls: This に限る means 'is the best choice' and voices the speaker's opinion; keep it apart from に限らず ('not limited to') and に限って ('of all ~').

examples.ja: 疲れた時は、寝るに限る。
examples.en: When you're tired, there's nothing like sleeping.
examples.f: ｜疲[つか]れた｜時[とき]は、｜寝[ね]るに｜限[かぎ]る。

examples.ja: 夏はやっぱり冷たいビールに限るね。
examples.en: In summer, you really can't beat a cold beer.
examples.f: ｜夏[なつ]はやっぱり｜冷[つめ]たいビールに｜限[かぎ]るね。

synonyms.note: 〜ほうがいい advises one option over another; に限る declares one thing simply the best.

related.note: に限らず means 'not just ~ (but also)'; に限る means '~ is the best'.
に限って means 'of all ~ (and no other)'; に限る means 'nothing beats ~'.

entry.title: に限らず
entry.meaning: not limited to; not just ~ but also
entry.summary: Noun＋に限らず says the statement is 'not limited to' the named noun but reaches more widely — 週末に限らず平日も ('not just on weekends but on weekdays too'). It broadens the scope beyond the single case, and usually a following 〜も／〜まで names the wider group it extends to.
pitfalls: Normally paired with a following 〜も or 〜まで that names the broader group the statement extends to.
に限らず broadens the scope ('not only N'); に限って narrows onto one specific N — the same 限 pulling opposite ways.

examples.ja: この公園は週末に限らず、平日もたくさんの人でにぎわっている。
examples.en: This park is crowded not just on weekends but on weekdays too.
examples.f: この｜公園[こうえん]は｜週末[しゅうまつ]に｜限[かぎ]らず、｜平日[へいじつ]もたくさんの｜人[ひと]でにぎわっている。

examples.ja: 最近は若者に限らず、幅広い世代がこのアプリを使っている。
examples.en: Lately it's not only young people — a wide range of generations use this app.
examples.f: ｜最近[さいきん]は｜若者[わかもの]に｜限[かぎ]らず、｜幅広[はばひろ]い｜世代[せだい]がこのアプリを｜使[つか]っている。

synonyms.note: のみならず also means 'not only ~ but also', in a more literary register; に限らず is a shade plainer.
だけでなく is the everyday 'not only ~ but also'; に限らず is slightly more formal and attaches straight to a noun.

antonyms.note: に限って singles out one specific N; に限らず insists the point is not limited to that N.

related.note: はもちろん takes the first item as obvious and adds more; に限らず simply denies that the scope stops at one item.

entry.title: に限って
entry.meaning: of all things/times; (that person) especially would not ~
entry.summary: Noun＋に限って singles out one specific noun with a nuance of irony or exception. With a following negative it defends a particular person or thing — うちの子に限ってそんなことはしない ('my child of all people would never do that'). With an event or time it complains that bad luck strikes at exactly the wrong moment — 急いでいる時に限って ('of all times, just when I'm in a hurry').
pitfalls: Two flavors: with a negative it defends a specific person or thing (あの人に限って…ない); with a time or event it grumbles that bad timing lines up (…時に限って).
Same 限 root as に限る ('is best') and に限らず ('not only'), but the meanings are different — don't blur them together.

examples.ja: 彼女に限って、そんな大事な約束を忘れるはずがありません。
examples.en: She of all people would never forget such an important promise.
examples.f: ｜彼女[かのじょ]に｜限[かぎ]って、そんな｜大事[だいじ]な｜約束[やくそく]を｜忘[わす]れるはずがありません。

examples.ja: 急いでいる時に限って、なかなかタクシーが来ない。
examples.en: It's exactly when I'm in a hurry that a taxi just won't come.
examples.f: ｜急[いそ]いでいる｜時[とき]に｜限[かぎ]って、なかなかタクシーが｜来[こ]ない。

antonyms.note: に限らず broadens ('not only N'); に限って narrows in on one specific N — opposite directions from the same 限.

related.note: に限る recommends N as the best choice; に限って singles N out with an ironic or defensive nuance.

entry.title: 限り
entry.meaning: as long as; as far as; within the limits of
entry.summary: 限り sets a boundary on a statement. Its main senses are 'as long as / so long as' a condition holds (Vる・Nである限り), and 'as far as' the speaker's information reaches (見る限り, 知る限り). The core idea is that the main clause is true only within the limit or scope named.
structure: Verb［dictionary form／ない form］＋ 限り
pitfalls: In the 'as long as' sense, the condition bounds the statement: once the condition ends, the claim no longer holds.
知る限り・見る限り mean 'as far as I know/can see', limiting a judgment to the information available, not making an absolute claim.

examples.ja: 私が知る限り、彼はそんなことをする人ではない。
examples.en: As far as I know, he is not the kind of person who would do such a thing.
examples.f: ｜私[わたし]が｜知[し]る｜限[かぎ]り、｜彼[かれ]はそんなことをする｜人[ひと]ではない。

examples.ja: 体が健康である限り、働き続けたい。
examples.en: As long as I stay healthy, I want to keep working.
examples.f: ｜体[からだ]が｜健康[けんこう]である｜限[かぎ]り、｜働[はたら]き｜続[つづ]けたい。

related.note: に限る comes from the same root but means 'nothing beats ~ / be limited to ~'; 限り sets the scope of a condition or judgment.
とは限らない, also from 限る, means 'not necessarily'; 限り marks the boundary within which a statement is valid.

entry.title: にかけては
entry.meaning: when it comes to (a skill someone excels at)
entry.summary: Noun＋にかけては singles out a field or skill and claims that, in that area, someone is second to none — 料理にかけては彼の右に出る者はいない ('when it comes to cooking, no one beats him'). The clause that follows almost always asserts excellence or confidence.
pitfalls: The following clause is normally positive — a claim of being the best or most confident; it does not fit neutral or negative statements.
Don't confuse it with にかけて ('from A over to B / spanning a range'); にかけては marks a domain of expertise.

examples.ja: 記憶力にかけては、クラスの誰にも負けない自信があります。
examples.en: When it comes to memory, I'm confident I won't lose to anyone in the class.
examples.f: ｜記憶[きおく]｜力[りょく]にかけては、クラスの｜誰[だれ]にも｜負[ま]けない｜自信[じしん]があります。

examples.ja: 速さにかけては、この選手が世界でトップだと言われている。
examples.en: When it comes to speed, this athlete is said to be the best in the world.
examples.f: ｜速[はや]さにかけては、この｜選手[せんしゅ]が｜世界[せかい]でトップだと｜言[い]われている。

related.note: にかけて marks a span from one point to another; にかけては marks the field in which someone excels.
において neutrally marks the sphere or setting; にかけては specifically frames it as a strength someone is best at.

entry.title: に応えて
entry.meaning: in response to; living up to (expectations/demand)
entry.summary: Noun＋に応えて means acting so as to meet or live up to something directed at you — expectations, a request, demand, or cheers. ファンの声援に応えて ('in response to the fans' cheers'). The noun is typically 期待・要望・要求・声援 — something the subject then satisfies.
pitfalls: It pairs with nouns of expectation or demand (期待・要望・要求・声援), not with just any noun.
応える here means 'to meet / live up to' (written 応), distinct from 答える 'to answer a question' — both read こたえる.

examples.ja: 消費者の要望に応えて、新しいサービスが始まった。
examples.en: In response to consumer demand, a new service was launched.
examples.f: ｜消費[しょうひ]｜者[しゃ]の｜要望[ようぼう]に｜応[こた]えて、｜新[あたら]しいサービスが｜始[はじ]まった。

examples.ja: 選手たちは、応援してくれた人々の期待に応えて優勝した。
examples.en: The players lived up to the expectations of those who cheered them on and won the championship.
examples.f: ｜選手[せんしゅ]たちは、｜応援[おうえん]してくれた｜人々[ひとびと]の｜期待[きたい]に｜応[こた]えて｜優勝[ゆうしょう]した。

related.note: に沿って means following a plan or wish without straying; に応えて means actively satisfying a demand aimed at you.
にしたがって means acting in obedience to an instruction; に応えて means fulfilling what others hope for from you.

entry.title: に相違ない
entry.meaning: without a doubt; there is no mistaking
entry.summary: に相違ない expresses the speaker's firm, reasoned conviction that something must be true — 'without a doubt; there's no mistaking it'. It is the formal, written-style counterpart of に違いない, common in essays, legal, and literary contexts.
structure: Verb／い-adjective［plain form］＋ に相違ない
pitfalls: Formal and written; in everyday speech に違いない (or casual に決まっている) is far more natural.
Attach directly to the plain form; no だ after a noun or な-adjective: 犯人に相違ない, not 犯人だに相違ない.

examples.ja: これだけの証拠がある以上、彼が犯人に相違ない。
examples.en: Given this much evidence, he is without a doubt the culprit.
examples.f: これだけの｜証拠[しょうこ]がある｜以上[いじょう]、｜彼[かれ]が｜犯人[はんにん]に｜相違[そうい]ない。

examples.ja: あの慌てた様子から見て、何か問題が起きたに相違ない。
examples.en: Judging from that flustered manner, something must certainly have gone wrong.
examples.f: あの｜慌[あわ]てた｜様子[ようす]から｜見[み]て、｜何[なに]か｜問題[もんだい]が｜起[お]きたに｜相違[そうい]ない。

synonyms.note: に違いない is the ordinary 'must be, no doubt'; に相違ない is its formal, written-register twin.
に決まっている is a casual, emotional 'obviously'; に相違ない is a formal, reasoned 'without a doubt'.

related.note: はずだ is a logical expectation open to revision; に相違ない asserts near-certainty with no room for doubt.

entry.title: に越したことはない
entry.meaning: there's nothing better than; it's best to ~
entry.summary: に越したことはない says a certain state is the ideal one to have, even if not strictly required — 用心するに越したことはない ('you can't go wrong being cautious'). It gently recommends the best option while allowing that the less-ideal alternative is still acceptable.
structure: Verb［dictionary form］＋ に越したことはない
い-adjective ＋ に越したことはない
Noun／な-adjective ＋（である）＋ に越したことはない
pitfalls: The nuance is 'it would be best / can't hurt', not a strict obligation — the less-ideal option still counts as fine.
It predicts a preference, so it pairs naturally with もし／〜なら ('if possible, it's best to…').

examples.ja: 旅行の予約は、早めにするに越したことはありません。
examples.en: When it comes to travel bookings, there's nothing better than doing it early.
examples.f: ｜旅行[りょこう]の｜予約[よやく]は、｜早[はや]めにするに｜越[こ]したことはありません。

examples.ja: 家から近いに越したことはないが、家賃も考える必要がある。
examples.en: You can't beat being close to home, but you also have to think about the rent.
examples.f: ｜家[いえ]から｜近[ちか]いに｜越[こ]したことはないが、｜家賃[やちん]も｜考[かんが]える｜必要[ひつよう]がある。

synonyms.note: に限る flatly declares N the best; に越したことはない softly recommends it while leaving room for other options.

related.note: ほうがいい gives a plain 'you'd better'; に越したことはない frames it as 'nothing beats it, though it isn't a must'.

entry.title: にほかならない
entry.meaning: is nothing but; is none other than
entry.summary: にほかならない attaches to a noun to declare emphatically that something is 'nothing other than' that noun — the speaker rules out every other explanation and insists this is the true identity or cause. 成功は努力の結果にほかならない = success is nothing but the fruit of effort. The tone is assertive and written.
pitfalls: It pins down a single, definitive identity or cause, and is far more insistent than a plain だ or である.
It attaches to nouns, including clauses nominalized with の／こと; it does not attach directly to a plain verb or adjective.

examples.ja: 今回の勝利は、チーム全員の努力の結果にほかならない。
examples.en: This victory is nothing other than the result of the whole team's effort.
examples.f: ｜今回[こんかい]の｜勝利[しょうり]は、チーム｜全員[ぜんいん]の｜努力[どりょく]の｜結果[けっか]にほかならない。

examples.ja: この決定は、住民の声を無視したものにほかならない。
examples.en: This decision is nothing but a disregard for the residents' voices.
examples.f: この｜決定[けってい]は、｜住民[じゅうみん]の｜声[こえ]を｜無視[むし]したものにほかならない。

related.note: に過ぎない shares the frame but downplays — 'no more than'; にほかならない elevates — 'precisely this and nothing else'.
こそ also singles something out emphatically as 'precisely'; にほかならない specifically equates a fact with its one true cause.

entry.title: にもかかわらず
entry.meaning: despite; even though; nevertheless
entry.summary: にもかかわらず means 'despite / even though' — the second clause happens contrary to what the first would lead you to expect. 雨にもかかわらず = despite the rain; 努力したにもかかわらず = even though (someone) tried hard. It attaches to nouns and to plain-form clauses, and carries a formal tone, often of surprise or dissatisfaction at the unexpected outcome.
structure: Sentence［plain form］＋ にもかかわらず
pitfalls: Do not confuse it with にかかわらず ('regardless of, whether or not'), which sets aside a range of options; にもかかわらず points to one fact that the result contradicts.
It is more formal than のに, and often colored with surprise or complaint at the unexpected result.

examples.ja: 十分に準備したにもかかわらず、試験の結果は思わしくなかった。
examples.en: Despite having prepared thoroughly, the exam results were not what I had hoped for.
examples.f: ｜十分[じゅうぶん]に｜準備[じゅんび]したにもかかわらず、｜試験[しけん]の｜結果[けっか]は｜思[おも]わしくなかった。

examples.ja: 悪天候にもかかわらず、多くの人が会場に集まった。
examples.en: In spite of the bad weather, many people gathered at the venue.
examples.f: ｜悪天候[あくてんこう]にもかかわらず、｜多[おお]くの｜人[ひと]が｜会場[かいじょう]に｜集[あつ]まった。

synonyms.note: のに also marks an unexpected, contrary result; にもかかわらず is more formal and written.
ものの also concedes 'although'; にもかかわらず stresses a result defying a clear expectation.

related.note: ながらも 'although' attaches to a stem or adjective and is more compact; にもかかわらず works after full clauses and nouns.

entry.title: にあたって・にあたり
entry.kana: にあたって・にあたり
entry.meaning: on the occasion of; at the time of (undertaking)
entry.summary: 〜にあたって・〜にあたり marks a significant moment — usually the start of an important undertaking — as the occasion for appropriate action. 開会にあたり = 'on the occasion of opening'. It is formal and forward-looking, used for milestones and ceremonies rather than everyday events. にあたって and にあたり are interchangeable, the latter a touch more formal.
structure: Verb［dictionary form］＋にあたって／にあたり
pitfalls: It suits significant, often formal occasions and the action taken for them; it isn't used for trivial daily events.
にあたって (て form) and にあたり (stem) mean the same thing; にあたり sounds slightly more formal and written.

examples.ja: 新規事業を始めるにあたって、まず市場を十分に調査した。
examples.en: In launching the new business, we first researched the market thoroughly.
examples.f: ｜新規[しんき]｜事業[じぎょう]を｜始[はじ]めるにあたって、まず｜市場[しじょう]を｜十分[じゅうぶん]に｜調査[ちょうさ]した。

examples.ja: 卒業にあたり、お世話になった先生に感謝の言葉を述べた。
examples.en: On the occasion of graduation, I expressed my thanks to the teachers who had helped me.
examples.f: ｜卒業[そつぎょう]にあたり、お｜世話[せわ]になった｜先生[せんせい]に｜感謝[かんしゃ]の｜言葉[ことば]を｜述[の]べた。

synonyms.note: に際して is very close ('on the occasion of'); にあたって leans toward preparing to undertake something, 際して toward a special moment or event.
に先立ち means 'prior to / in advance of', stressing timing before the event; にあたって marks the occasion itself.

related.note: 上で is a more procedural 'in the course of / when doing'; にあたって singles out an important occasion.

entry.title: にかかわらず
entry.meaning: regardless of; whether or not; irrespective of
entry.summary: 〜にかかわらず means a result holds no matter which of the possibilities applies. It attaches to a noun (天候にかかわらず) or to a paired affirmative-and-negative (参加するしないにかかわらず, 有無にかかわらず). The point is that variation in the condition makes no difference to the outcome.
structure: Verb／い-adjective［affirmative + negative pair］＋にかかわらず
pitfalls: にかかわらず ('regardless of') is not にもかかわらず ('despite the fact that'); the latter concedes a real, established fact.
It often pairs opposite options — 行く行かず, 好き嫌い, 大小 — meaning the result is the same either way.

examples.ja: 天候にかかわらず、大会は予定どおり行われます。
examples.en: Regardless of the weather, the tournament will be held as scheduled.
examples.f: ｜天候[てんこう]にかかわらず、｜大会[たいかい]は｜予定[よてい]どおり｜行[おこな]われます。

examples.ja: 経験の有無にかかわらず、どなたでも応募できます。
examples.en: Anyone may apply, whether or not they have experience.
examples.f: ｜経験[けいけん]の｜有無[うむ]にかかわらず、どなたでも｜応募[おうぼ]できます。

synonyms.note: を問わず also means 'regardless of / irrespective of'; both are formal, with を問わず common in notices (年齢を問わず).

related.note: にもかかわらず means 'despite', conceding a real fact; にかかわらず means 'no matter which', with no fact conceded.
によらず likewise means 'regardless of / not depending on'; にかかわらず often pairs opposite options for 'either way'.

entry.title: に関わる
entry.meaning: to concern; to affect; to have a serious bearing on
entry.summary: 〜に関わる means to have a weighty bearing on something important — life, honor, credibility, a future. 命に関わる = 'a matter of life and death'; 信用に関わる問題 = 'an issue that affects one's credibility'. It implies serious stakes, not a casual 'about', and often modifies the noun that follows.
pitfalls: It implies a serious, high-stakes bearing (命・名誉・信用); for the neutral 'concerning / about', use に関して or について.
Don't confuse it with にかかわらず ('regardless of'), which shares the 関わ root but has the opposite grammatical role.

examples.ja: これは会社の信用に関わる重大な問題です。
examples.en: This is a grave matter that affects the company's credibility.
examples.f: これは｜会社[かいしゃ]の｜信用[しんよう]に｜関[かか]わる｜重大[じゅうだい]な｜問題[もんだい]です。

examples.ja: 少しの油断が命に関わることもある。
examples.en: A moment's carelessness can be a matter of life and death.
examples.f: ｜少[すこ]しの｜油断[ゆだん]が｜命[いのち]に｜関[かか]わることもある。

related.note: に関して・に関する is the neutral 'concerning / about (a topic)'; に関わる implies a serious, high-stakes bearing.
について is a plain 'about ~'; に関わる means something critically affects the matter, not merely relates to it.
にかかわらず ('regardless of') shares the 関わ root but flips the grammar to 'no matter ~', not 'affects ~'.

entry.title: につき
entry.meaning: due to; per; each
entry.summary: につき has two main uses. As 'due to', it gives a reason in formal notices — 本日は定休日につき休業します ('as today is a regular holiday, we are closed'). As 'per', it states a rate — 一つにつき百円 ('100 yen each'). Both are set, somewhat formal uses of the same につき.
pitfalls: The 'due to' sense is formal and written — typical of signs and announcements, not casual speech (use から／ので there).
Tell the two senses apart by context: reason (定休日につき) versus rate (ひとりにつき).

examples.ja: 準備中につき、しばらくお待ちください。
examples.en: As we are still preparing, please wait a while.
examples.f: ｜準備[じゅんび]｜中[ちゅう]につき、しばらくお｜待[ま]ちください。

examples.ja: この商品は、おひとりにつき三つまで購入できます。
examples.en: You may buy up to three of this item per person.
examples.f: この｜商品[しょうひん]は、おひとりにつき｜三[みっ]つまで｜購入[こうにゅう]できます。

synonyms.note: 当たり covers the 'per unit' rate sense; につき shares that sense but also means 'due to', which 当たり never does.

related.note: ために gives a reason in ordinary registers; につき in its 'due to' sense is the stiffer, notice-style equivalent.

entry.title: を込めて
entry.meaning: putting (feeling or effort) into; filled with ~
entry.summary: を込めて attaches to a noun naming a feeling or energy and says the following action is carried out with that feeling poured into it — 心を込めて = with all one's heart, 感謝を込めて = with gratitude. The noun names the emotion or effort that fills the act.
pitfalls: The noun names a feeling or energy put into the act (心, 愛, 感謝, 願い); it is not used for physically filling a container with something.
Don't mix it up with だらけ ('covered in / full of'), which describes a surface littered with something unwanted; を込めて is about pouring emotion into an action, even though both can be glossed 'full of'.

examples.ja: 母に感謝を込めて手紙を書きました。
examples.en: I wrote a letter to my mother with heartfelt gratitude.
examples.f: ｜母[はは]に｜感謝[かんしゃ]を｜込[こ]めて｜手紙[てがみ]を｜書[か]きました。

examples.ja: 彼女は心を込めて歌を歌った。
examples.en: She sang the song with all her heart.
examples.f: ｜彼女[かのじょ]は｜心[こころ]を｜込[こ]めて｜歌[うた]を｜歌[うた]った。

related.note: 〜だらけ means a surface is covered in or full of something (usually unwanted); を込めて is about putting feeling into an action.

entry.title: を中心に
entry.meaning: centered on; with ~ at the center; mainly among ~
entry.summary: を中心に（して） marks the thing that sits at the center of some activity, group, or arrangement — everything else gathers around it or is organized with it as the focus. 駅を中心に = centered on the station; 若者を中心に = mainly among young people.
structure: Noun ＋ を中心とした ＋ Noun
pitfalls: を中心に marks the focal point that other things arrange themselves around; it isn't a plain 'about (a topic)' — for simply discussing a subject, use について.

examples.ja: この町では、駅を中心に店が並んでいます。
examples.en: In this town, the shops are lined up centered around the station.
examples.f: この｜町[まち]では、｜駅[えき]を｜中心[ちゅうしん]に｜店[みせ]が｜並[なら]んでいます。

examples.ja: その歌手は若い人を中心に人気があります。
examples.en: That singer is popular mainly among young people.
examples.f: その｜歌手[かしゅ]は｜若[わか]い｜人[ひと]を｜中心[ちゅうしん]に｜人気[にんき]があります。

related.note: をめぐって centers a dispute or discussion around an issue; を中心に marks a focal point things are arranged around, without the sense of contention.
について marks the topic you talk or think about; を中心に marks what sits at the center of an activity or group.

entry.title: をもとに
entry.meaning: based on; on the basis of; drawing on
entry.summary: をもとに(して) / をもとにした marks the material, source, or reference used to create or judge something — 'based on, drawing on'. The following action builds on that source as its foundation: 事件をもとに作った映画 = 'a film made based on the incident'. Use をもとにした before a noun.
structure: Noun ＋ をもとにした ＋ Noun
pitfalls: The source is raw material you build or judge from (data, a story, experience), so the following clause is usually one of creating or evaluating.
Compare に基づいて, which stresses conforming to a rule or principle; をもとに stresses using something as source material.

examples.ja: この映画は、実際に起きた事件をもとに作られたそうだ。
examples.en: This film was apparently made based on an incident that really happened.
examples.f: この｜映画[えいが]は、｜実際[じっさい]に｜起[お]きた｜事件[じけん]をもとに｜作[つく]られたそうだ。

examples.ja: アンケートの結果をもとに、新商品の改良を進めた。
examples.en: Drawing on the survey results, we went ahead with improvements to the new product.
examples.f: アンケートの｜結果[けっか]をもとに、｜新[しん]｜商品[しょうひん]の｜改良[かいりょう]を｜進[すす]めた。

synonyms.note: に基づいて also means 'based on', but emphasizes acting in accordance with a rule or principle rather than using source material.

entry.title: を問わず
entry.meaning: regardless of; irrespective of
entry.summary: を問わず attaches to a noun to say something applies without regard to that factor — 'regardless of, irrespective of'. It typically follows a noun naming a variable (年齢, 経験) or a pair of opposites (男女, 昼夜), and the statement then holds true across all of them. It is formal in tone.
pitfalls: It takes a noun (a category, variable, or pair of opposites), not a clause or a か-question.
It is formal and written; にかかわらず is broader in what it can attach to and slightly less formal.

examples.ja: この仕事は経験を問わず、やる気のある人を歓迎します。
examples.en: This job welcomes motivated people regardless of experience.
examples.f: この｜仕事[しごと]は｜経験[けいけん]を｜問[と]わず、やる｜気[き]のある｜人[ひと]を｜歓迎[かんげい]します。

examples.ja: そのカフェは、季節を問わず多くの観光客でにぎわっている。
examples.en: That cafe bustles with tourists regardless of the season.
examples.f: そのカフェは、｜季節[きせつ]を｜問[と]わず｜多[おお]くの｜観光[かんこう]｜客[きゃく]でにぎわっている。

synonyms.note: にかかわらず also means 'regardless of' but attaches more freely, including to plain forms and か-questions.
いかんにかかわらず means 'regardless of what X is'; it is more formal and rigid than を問わず.

entry.title: をはじめ
entry.meaning: starting with ~; ~ and others like it; headed by ~
entry.summary: をはじめ（として） singles out one representative, usually the most prominent, member of a group and implies a wider set follows it — X and others like it. 東京をはじめ、大都市では… = In big cities, starting with Tokyo… The named item heads a list that isn't spelled out in full.
structure: Noun ＋ をはじめとする ＋ Noun
pitfalls: The noun before をはじめ is the leading, most representative member of a group, not just a random example; it heads the list rather than being tucked into it.

examples.ja: この店では、りんごをはじめ、いろいろな果物を売っています。
examples.en: This shop sells all kinds of fruit, starting with apples.
examples.f: この｜店[みせ]では、りんごをはじめ、いろいろな｜果物[くだもの]を｜売[う]っています。

examples.ja: 校長先生をはじめ、多くの先生が卒業式に出席しました。
examples.en: Many teachers, headed by the principal, attended the graduation ceremony.
examples.f: ｜校長[こうちょう]｜先生[せんせい]をはじめ、｜多[おお]くの｜先生[せんせい]が｜卒業[そつぎょう]｜式[しき]に｜出席[しゅっせき]しました。

synonyms.note: など lists an item as one example among others ('and so on'); をはじめ presents its noun as the leading member the rest follow.

related.note: とか〜とか lists a couple of casual examples side by side; をはじめ names one prominent member standing in for a larger group.

entry.title: か〜ないかのうちに
entry.romaji: ka ~ nai ka no uchi ni
entry.meaning: no sooner had ~ than; the moment ~; barely had X happened when Y
entry.summary: This pattern repeats one verb — first in the dictionary form, then in the ない form — to say that a second event happens almost the very instant the first does: 'X had barely happened when Y'. The two events are nearly simultaneous, and Y typically follows on immediately.
structure: Verb［dictionary form］＋ か ＋ Verb［ない form］＋ か ＋ のうちに
pitfalls: The two verbs must be the same verb, one affirmative and one negative: 着くか着かないかのうちに.
It describes near-simultaneous events observed by the speaker, so the main clause states something that follows right away, not a plan.

examples.ja: ベルが鳴るか鳴らないかのうちに、生徒たちは教室を飛び出した。
examples.en: The bell had barely rung when the students dashed out of the classroom.
examples.f: ベルが｜鳴[な]るか｜鳴[な]らないかのうちに、｜生徒[せいと]たちは｜教室[きょうしつ]を｜飛び出[とびだ]した。

examples.ja: 彼はベッドに入るか入らないかのうちに、眠ってしまった。
examples.en: He was barely in bed when he fell fast asleep.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]はベッドに｜入[はい]るか｜入[はい]らないかのうちに、｜眠[ねむ]ってしまった。

synonyms.note: た途端 also marks 'the moment after', but follows a past-tense verb; this pattern stresses that the first action had barely finished.
が早いか is a more literary 'as soon as'; か〜ないかのうちに emphasizes the two events overlapping almost to the instant.

related.note: かと思ったら also links two quick events, but adds surprise that the second is unexpected; this pattern is purely about timing.

entry.title: きり
entry.meaning: only; just; (after た-form) ~ and nothing since
entry.summary: きり has two senses: after a noun it means 'only, just' (二人きり = just the two of us), and after a た-form verb it means 'since ~, and nothing has changed since' (出かけたきり = went out and hasn't come back). Both narrow things down to a single case.
pitfalls: With a た-form it implies the expected next action never followed: 寝たきり = bedridden (lay down and stayed that way).
In the 'only' sense it overlaps with だけ but feels more exclusive and is a bit colloquial.

examples.ja: 彼とは一度会ったきり、その後会っていない。
examples.en: I met him just once, and I haven't seen him since.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]とは｜一度[いちど]｜会[あ]ったきり、その｜後[ご]｜会[あ]っていない。

examples.ja: 祖母は病気で、もう何年も寝たきりだ。
examples.en: My grandmother is ill and has been bedridden for years now.
examples.f: ｜祖母[そぼ]は｜病気[びょうき]で、もう｜何[なん]｜年[ねん]も｜寝[ね]たきりだ。

synonyms.note: だけ 'only' is the neutral limiter; きり is more exclusive/colloquial and also has the た-form 'since' use.

related.note: ばかり 'nothing but / just' overlaps in the 'only' sense; きり adds the 'and nothing since' meaning.

entry.title: 〜げ
entry.meaning: looking ~; with an air of ~ (seeming)
entry.summary: 〜げ attaches to an adjective stem, or to the stem of 〜たい, to form a な-adjective/adverb meaning 'looking ~, with an air of ~'. 寂しげ = looking lonely, 自慢げ = with a boastful air, 言いたげ = as if wanting to say something. It describes the outward impression a person gives off, usually about their feelings.
pitfalls: Drop the final い of an い-adjective: 寂しい → 寂しげ, not 寂しいげ.
It reports an outward impression the person seems to give, not a firm claim about their true feelings.
It attaches only to a limited set of feeling/appearance words; you can't append it freely to any adjective.

examples.ja: 彼女は何か言いたげな表情でこちらを見ていた。
examples.en: She was looking my way with an expression as if she wanted to say something.
examples.f: ｜彼女[かのじょ]は｜何[なに]か｜言[い]いたげな｜表情[ひょうじょう]でこちらを｜見[み]ていた。

examples.ja: 子供たちは自慢げに賞状を見せてくれた。
examples.en: The children showed me their certificates with an air of pride.
examples.f: ｜子供[こども]たちは｜自慢[じまん]げに｜賞状[しょうじょう]を｜見[み]せてくれた。

synonyms.note: そうな reports how something looks generally; 〜げ centers on the air a person gives off, especially about feelings.
っぽい says something has a ~ quality or tendency; 〜げ is specifically 'seeming / looking'.

entry.title: っこない
entry.meaning: there's no chance of ~; definitely won't / can't
entry.summary: っこない attaches to the ます-stem to flatly deny that something could ever happen — 分かりっこない = 'there's no way I'd understand', 勝てっこない = 'we can't possibly win'. It is a casual, spoken way to voice the speaker's firm conviction that something is impossible, close in meaning to はずがない but far more colloquial.
pitfalls: Attach it to the ます-stem, not the dictionary form: 勝てっこない, not 勝つっこない.
It belongs to casual, spoken Japanese; avoid it in formal writing, where はずがない or わけがない fit better.
It states the speaker's own strong belief that something is impossible, not an objective fact.

examples.ja: 宝くじなんて、そう簡単に当たりっこないよ。
examples.en: There's no way you'll win the lottery that easily.
examples.f: ｜宝[たから]くじなんて、そう｜簡単[かんたん]に｜当[あ]たりっこないよ。

examples.ja: いくら急いでも、終電に間に合いっこない。
examples.en: No matter how much I hurry, there's no chance I'll make the last train.
examples.f: いくら｜急[いそ]いでも、｜終電[しゅうでん]に｜間に合[まにあ]いっこない。

synonyms.note: わけがない also denies possibility but is neutral in register; っこない is distinctly casual and spoken.
はずがない reasons that something 'can't be so'; っこない is a blunter, colloquial 'no way it'll happen'.

related.note: まい is a formal/written negative conjecture ('surely won't'); っこない carries the same certainty in casual speech.

entry.title: どころか
entry.meaning: far from; let alone; not to mention; on the contrary
entry.summary: どころか denies one idea and replaces it with something further off. In one use, reality is the opposite of what was suggested — 謝るどころか、もっと怒り出した = far from apologizing, he got even angrier. In the other, it rules out a smaller thing to stress a bigger one — 漢字どころか、ひらがなも読めない = he can't read hiragana, let alone kanji. Either way, what comes after is more extreme.
structure: な-adjective［plain form］／い-adjective／Verb［plain form］＋ どころか
pitfalls: The second half must go beyond or reverse the first; it's not a neutral 'and also' — for plain addition use だけでなく.
In the 'let alone' pattern the easier or smaller item comes first, and the more surprising one follows with も.

examples.ja: 彼は漢字どころか、ひらがなも読めない。
examples.en: He can't even read hiragana, let alone kanji.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]は｜漢字[かんじ]どころか、ひらがなも｜読[よ]めない。

examples.ja: 薬を飲んだのに、よくなるどころか熱が上がった。
examples.en: I took the medicine, but far from getting better my fever went up.
examples.f: ｜薬[くすり]を｜飲[の]んだのに、よくなるどころか｜熱[ねつ]が｜上[あ]がった。

synonyms.note: ばかりか adds a further, heavier point ('not only ... but even'); どころか can also flatly reverse the expectation.

related.note: むしろ says 'rather, if anything'; どころか denies the first idea outright and pushes to the opposite or beyond.

entry.title: どころではない
entry.meaning: this is no time for ~; ~ is out of the question
entry.summary: どころではない says the circumstances make something out of the question — 'this is no time for ~ / I'm in no position to ~'. 忙しくて旅行どころではない = 'I'm too busy — a trip is out of the question'. It strongly rejects an activity as impossible given more pressing conditions.
structure: Verb［dictionary form］＋ どころではない
pitfalls: Don't confuse it with どころか ('far from ~; on the contrary'), which contrasts an expectation with a stronger reality; どころではない rules an activity out due to circumstances.
The rejected activity is usually something minor compared with the pressing situation that overrides it.

examples.ja: 仕事が山ほどあって、昼ご飯を食べるどころではない。
examples.en: I have a mountain of work — eating lunch is out of the question.
examples.f: ｜仕事[しごと]が｜山[やま]ほどあって、｜昼[ひる]ご｜飯[はん]を｜食[た]べるどころではない。

examples.ja: 大きな地震の直後で、旅行どころではなかった。
examples.en: Right after the big earthquake, a trip was out of the question.
examples.f: ｜大[おお]きな｜地震[じしん]の｜直後[ちょくご]で、｜旅行[りょこう]どころではなかった。

related.note: どころか contrasts expectation with a stronger reality ('far from ~'); どころではない says circumstances make something impossible.

entry.title: とは限らない
entry.meaning: not necessarily; it isn't always the case that ~
entry.summary: Sentence［plain form］＋ とは限らない pushes back on a general assumption, saying it doesn't always hold — 高いものが必ずいいとは限らない = expensive things aren't necessarily good. It admits the idea is often true while denying that it's always true. It pairs naturally with 必ずしも ('not always') earlier in the sentence.
structure: Sentence［plain form］＋ とは限らない
pitfalls: It means 'not always', not 'never': it allows exceptions rather than denying the idea outright.
It often teams up with 必ずしも for emphasis: 必ずしも〜とは限らない.

examples.ja: 高いものが、必ずしもいいとは限らない。
examples.en: Expensive things aren't necessarily good.
examples.f: ｜高[たか]いものが、｜必[かなら]ずしもいいとは｜限[かぎ]らない。

examples.ja: たくさん練習したからといって、試合に勝てるとは限らない。
examples.en: Practicing a lot doesn't necessarily mean you'll win the match.
examples.f: たくさん｜練習[れんしゅう]したからといって、｜試合[しあい]に｜勝[か]てるとは｜限[かぎ]らない。

related.note: 必ずしも is the adverb 'not always' that often sets up this pattern; とは限らない is the ending that denies a blanket rule.
わけではない denies a conclusion drawn from the situation; とは限らない denies that a general rule always holds.

entry.title: というものだ
entry.meaning: that really is ~; that's what you call ~ (emphatic assertion)
entry.summary: というものだ makes an emphatic, often evaluative assertion about the true nature of something — 'that really is ~ / that's what you call ~'. 助け合うのが友情というものだ = 'helping each other is what friendship truly is'. The speaker states a general truth or firm judgment, frequently with a reflective or critical tone.
structure: Sentence［plain form］＋ というものだ
pitfalls: Don't confuse it with the negative というものではない ('it's not necessarily so'); というものだ affirms strongly.
It voices conviction about how something essentially is, not a neutral description of a single event.

examples.ja: 困ったときに助け合うのが、本当の友情というものだ。
examples.en: Helping each other in hard times — that's what true friendship really is.
examples.f: ｜困[こま]ったときに｜助け合[たすけあ]うのが、｜本当[ほんとう]の｜友情[ゆうじょう]というものだ。

examples.ja: 締め切りを守らないのは、社会人として無責任というものだ。
examples.en: Failing to meet deadlines is, for a working adult, truly irresponsible.
examples.f: ｜締め切[しめき]りを｜守[まも]らないのは、｜社会[しゃかい]｜人[じん]として｜無責任[むせきにん]というものだ。

synonyms.note: ものだ states general truths or 'should' advice; というものだ frames a stronger, evaluative assertion about a thing's essential nature.

antonyms.note: というものではない is the direct counter — 'it's not necessarily the case that ~'.

entry.title: まい
entry.meaning: surely won't ~; I have no intention of ~ (literary negative)
entry.summary: まい is a literary negative auxiliary with two senses: negative conjecture ('surely won't / probably not', ≈ ないだろう) and negative volition ('I will not / I refuse to', ≈ しないつもりだ). It attaches to the dictionary form; with ichidan verbs and する the stem is also used (見まい／すまい). It sounds formal or old-fashioned.
structure: する → するまい／すまい、来る → 来るまい／来まい
pitfalls: Two meanings: with a third person it is usually 'surely won't' (conjecture); with the speaker it is 'I won't / I refuse' (volition).
It is literary; everyday Japanese uses ないだろう for the guess and ないつもりだ for the intention.

examples.ja: こんな失敗は二度とするまいと、心に決めた。
examples.en: I resolved never to make this kind of mistake again.
examples.f: こんな｜失敗[しっぱい]は｜二度[にど]とするまいと、｜心[こころ]に｜決[き]めた。

examples.ja: 彼女ほどの実力があれば、この試験に落ちることはあるまい。
examples.en: With ability like hers, surely she won't fail this exam.
examples.f: ｜彼女[かのじょ]ほどの｜実力[じつりょく]があれば、この｜試験[しけん]に｜落[お]ちることはあるまい。

antonyms.note: ようと思う states the intention to do something; まい (volitional sense) states the intention not to.

related.note: だろう is positive conjecture ('probably will'); まい is its negative literary counterpart ('surely won't').
べきではない says one shouldn't (obligation); まい voices the speaker's own resolve not to, or a negative guess.

entry.title: もかまわず
entry.meaning: without caring about ~; heedless of ~; paying no mind to ~
entry.summary: 〜もかまわず (も構わず) means acting without concern for something that would normally give one pause — 人目もかまわず ('heedless of others' eyes'). The doer goes ahead despite X, ignoring what X would ordinarily demand.
structure: Sentence ＋ の ＋ もかまわず
pitfalls: X もかまわず means the doer disregards X, usually something they arguably should mind (人目, 服が汚れるの); it is not a neutral 'regardless'.
構う here is in the negative ず-form, and the phrase is fixed as 〜もかまわず.

examples.ja: 彼女は人目もかまわず、大声で泣き出した。
examples.en: Heedless of the people around her, she burst into loud tears.
examples.f: ｜彼女[かのじょ]は｜人目[ひとめ]もかまわず、｜大声[おおごえ]で｜泣[な]き｜出[だ]した。

examples.ja: 彼は服が汚れるのもかまわず、子供と一緒に地面に座った。
examples.en: Not caring that his clothes would get dirty, he sat down on the ground with the children.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]は｜服[ふく]が｜汚[よご]れるのもかまわず、｜子供[こども]と｜一緒[いっしょ]に｜地面[じめん]に｜座[すわ]った。

related.note: にもかかわらず means 'despite (a fact)'; もかまわず stresses that the doer pays X no mind.
を問わず means 'regardless of which/any'; もかまわず means acting without heeding one specific concern.

entry.title: 〜上
entry.meaning: from the standpoint of ~; in terms of ~; for ~ reasons
entry.summary: Noun＋上 (じょう) means 'from the standpoint of ~ / in terms of ~' — 法律上 = legally, 健康上 = for health reasons, 立場上 = given one's position. It frames the following statement within that particular domain or consideration. It attaches to a limited set of abstract nouns.
pitfalls: This 上 reads じょう and means 'in terms of ~'; it is not うえ ('on top of / after').
It attaches only to a restricted set of abstract nouns (歴史上, 経験上, 教育上); you can't append it to any noun freely.

examples.ja: その計画は予算上、実現が難しい。
examples.en: That plan is hard to realize in budgetary terms.
examples.f: その｜計画[けいかく]は｜予算[よさん]｜上[じょう]、｜実現[じつげん]が｜難[むずか]しい。

examples.ja: 立場上、私からは何も申し上げられません。
examples.en: Given my position, there is nothing I can say.
examples.f: ｜立場[たちば]｜上[じょう]、｜私[わたし]からは｜何[なに]も｜申し上[もうしあ]げられません。

synonyms.note: 的 turns a noun into '~-wise / in terms of ~' broadly; 〜上 is limited to fixed nouns and often means 'from the standpoint of'.

related.note: 上で reads うえで and means 'upon doing / in the course of'; the same kanji, but a different reading and meaning.

entry.title: 恐れがある
entry.meaning: there is a risk/danger that (something undesirable may happen)
entry.summary: 恐れがある follows a verb (dictionary form) or a noun + の and warns that there is a real risk of an undesirable outcome. It is formal and largely written — common in news reports, warnings, and forecasts. 恐れ literally means 'fear', so it points to something one would rather avoid.
structure: Noun ＋ の ＋ 恐れがある
pitfalls: Used only for unwelcome outcomes; you would not say 合格する恐れがある for a hoped-for result.
Formal and written; in everyday speech かもしれない sounds more natural.

examples.ja: 台風の影響で、明日は電車が止まる恐れがあります。
examples.en: Because of the typhoon, there is a risk the trains will stop tomorrow.
examples.f: ｜台風[たいふう]の｜影響[えいきょう]で、｜明日[あした]は｜電車[でんしゃ]が｜止[と]まる｜恐[おそ]れがあります。

examples.ja: 誤った使い方をすると、事故につながる恐れがある。
examples.en: If it is used incorrectly, there is a danger it could lead to an accident.
examples.f: ｜誤[あやま]った｜使い方[つかいかた]をすると、｜事故[じこ]につながる｜恐[おそ]れがある。

synonyms.note: かねない also flags a possible bad outcome but attaches to a verb stem and is less formal; 恐れがある reads as an objective warning.

related.note: かもしれない is a neutral 'might', for good or bad; 恐れがある specifically warns of an undesirable risk.

entry.title: せいか
entry.meaning: perhaps because; maybe owing to
entry.summary: せいか marks a cause the speaker suspects but is not certain of — せい names a cause and か adds 'perhaps'. It is often used for an unexpected or unwelcome result whose reason is only a guess: 年のせいか = 'maybe because of my age'. The tone is tentative rather than assertive.
pitfalls: A noun takes の (寒さのせいか) and a な-adjective takes な before せいか.
Unlike せいで, which states the cause as a fact, せいか only guesses at it — it usually accompanies a tentative statement.

examples.ja: 疲れていたせいか、話の内容をよく覚えていない。
examples.en: Perhaps because I was tired, I don't remember the content of the talk very well.
examples.f: ｜疲[つか]れていたせいか、｜話[はなし]の｜内容[ないよう]をよく｜覚[おぼ]えていない。

examples.ja: 天気が悪かったせいか、来場者はいつもより少なかった。
examples.en: Maybe because the weather was bad, there were fewer visitors than usual.
examples.f: ｜天気[てんき]が｜悪[わる]かったせいか、｜来場[らいじょう]｜者[しゃ]はいつもより｜少[すく]なかった。

synonyms.note: せいで states the (usually negative) cause as a definite fact; せいか only suspects it.

related.note: おかげで credits a good result to a cause; せいか is neutral-to-negative and merely tentative.
ために plainly states 'because of', with no doubt or blame; せいか adds uncertainty.

entry.title: だけのことはある
entry.meaning: no wonder; it's not for nothing; it lives up to it
entry.summary: Placed at the end of a sentence, だけのことはある confirms that a result matches the effort, training, or reputation behind it — 'no wonder; it really shows'. It expresses admiration that something has earned its outcome. The shortened 〜だけある is also common.
structure: Verb・い-adjective・な-adjective［plain form］／Noun ＋ だけのことはある
pitfalls: It typically closes the sentence as a comment on a result; だけあって and だけに instead lead into the result mid-sentence.

examples.ja: 毎日練習しているだけのことはある。彼のピアノは本当に上手だ。
examples.en: It's not for nothing that he practices every day — his piano is truly excellent.
examples.f: ｜毎日[まいにち]｜練習[れんしゅう]しているだけのことはある。｜彼[かれ]のピアノは｜本当[ほんとう]に｜上手[じょうず]だ。

examples.ja: この料理は、さすが一流の店だけのことはある。
examples.en: This dish really lives up to the first-class restaurant it comes from.
examples.f: この｜料理[りょうり]は、さすが｜一流[いちりゅう]の｜店[みせ]だけのことはある。

synonyms.note: だけあって leads into the praised result mid-sentence; だけのことはある delivers it as a closing verdict.
だけに means 'all the more because' and can turn negative; だけのことはある is purely admiring approval.

related.note: さすが is a standalone marker of admiration; だけのことはある spells out that the result was earned.

entry.title: たとえ〜ても
entry.meaning: even if (hypothetically) ...
entry.summary: たとえ〜ても sets up a hypothetical and says the result holds no matter what — "even if." The たとえ at the front signals early that a supposition is coming, and it pairs with a following ても. It stresses that the outcome won't change.
structure: たとえ ＋ Verb［て form］＋ も
pitfalls: たとえ needs a matching ても／でも later in the sentence; don't leave it hanging.
たとえ ('even if') is a different word from 例えば ('for example') — don't swap them.

examples.ja: たとえ雨が降っても、試合は行われます。
examples.en: Even if it rains, the match will be held.
examples.f: たとえ｜雨[あめ]が｜降[ふ]っても、｜試合[しあい]は｜行[おこな]われます。

examples.ja: たとえ失敗しても、挑戦したことに意味がある。
examples.en: Even if I fail, there's meaning in having taken on the challenge.
examples.f: たとえ｜失敗[しっぱい]しても、｜挑戦[ちょうせん]したことに｜意味[いみ]がある。

synonyms.note: ても alone can mean 'even if'; たとえ〜ても adds an explicit, emphatic 'suppose that ...' at the front.

related.note: たって is a casual spoken 'even if'; たとえ〜ても is the standard, emphatic hypothetical.

entry.title: やら〜やら
entry.meaning: what with ... and ... (and other things)
entry.summary: やら〜やら lists two representative items — nouns, verbs, or adjectives — while implying there are others besides. It often carries a nuance of things being troublesome, chaotic, or overwhelming, so it suits situations of busyness or mixed feelings: 荷物やら書類やら = 'what with luggage and papers and all'.
structure: Noun ＋ やら ＋ Noun ＋ やら
Verb／Adjective［plain form］＋ やら ＋ Verb／Adjective［plain form］＋ やら
pitfalls: It tends to convey that the listed things pile up into something troublesome or confusing, unlike the neutral listing of とか.
The items should be of the same type (two nouns, two adjectives), and the pattern implies 'and others', not an exhaustive list.

examples.ja: 引っ越しの日は、荷造りやら手続きやらで一日じゅうばたばたしていた。
examples.en: On moving day, what with the packing and the paperwork and everything, I was in a rush the whole day.
examples.f: ｜引っ越[ひっこ]しの｜日[ひ]は、｜荷造[にづく]りやら｜手続[てつづ]きやらで｜一[いち]｜日[にち]じゅうばたばたしていた。

examples.ja: 合格の知らせを聞いて、うれしいやら信じられないやら、複雑な気持ちだった。
examples.en: Hearing I had passed, I felt happy and disbelieving and all sorts of things — it was a complicated feeling.
examples.f: ｜合格[ごうかく]の｜知[し]らせを｜聞[き]いて、うれしいやら｜信[しん]じられないやら、｜複雑[ふくざつ]な｜気持[きも]ちだった。

synonyms.note: とか〜とか lists examples neutrally; やら〜やら adds a sense of trouble, disorder, or being overwhelmed.

related.note: 〜たり〜たり lists representative actions neutrally; やら〜やら lists items with an exasperated or busy nuance.

entry.title: ようによっては
entry.meaning: depending on how one does or looks at it
entry.summary: ようによっては is 'manner' よう (verb stem + よう, as in 考えよう・使いよう) followed by によっては 'depending on'. It says that a different — often more favorable — result is possible depending on the way you approach or interpret something. 考えようによっては = depending on how you look at it; 使いようによっては = depending on how you use it. It frequently introduces a reframing that turns a seemingly negative thing into something acceptable.
pitfalls: This よう is the 'way/manner' nominalizer (考えよう, 言いよう), not the volitional; don't read it as ようにも or ようとする.
It usually sets up a positive reframing — 'seen a certain way, it's actually fine' — rather than a neutral list of possibilities.

examples.ja: 考えようによっては、この失敗も貴重な経験だと言える。
examples.en: Depending on how you look at it, even this failure can be called a valuable experience.
examples.f: ｜考[かんが]えようによっては、この｜失敗[しっぱい]も｜貴重[きちょう]な｜経験[けいけん]だと｜言[い]える。

examples.ja: 言いようによっては、相手を傷つけずに断ることもできる。
examples.en: Depending on how you phrase it, you can turn someone down without hurting them.
examples.f: ｜言[い]いようによっては、｜相手[あいて]を｜傷[きず]つけずに｜断[ことわ]ることもできる。

related.note: Both use よう, but ようにも〜ない is the volitional ('even if I try'); ようによっては is the manner noun ('depending on the way').

entry.title: 〜がてら
entry.meaning: while; on the same occasion as; taking the opportunity of
entry.summary: 〜がてら marks doing two things on one occasion, typically while going somewhere: you set out to do A and, on the same trip, also do B. 散歩がてら (while out for a walk), 買い物に行きがてら (on the way to shop). It attaches to a suru-noun or a verb stem. A is the nominal reason for the outing and B is folded in along the way — lighter and more everyday than the formal かたがた.
pitfalls: One single occasion, usually involving going somewhere; the two actions share the same trip.
Attaches to a noun or verb stem — 行きがてら, not 行くがてら.
More casual than かたがた, which is reserved for formal social acts.

examples.ja: 散歩がてら、駅前に新しくできたパン屋をのぞいてみた。
examples.en: While out for a walk, I popped into the new bakery that had opened in front of the station.
examples.f: ｜散歩[さんぽ]がてら、｜駅前[えきまえ]に｜新[あたら]しくできたパン｜屋[や]をのぞいてみた。

examples.ja: 買い物に行きがてら、借りていた本を図書館に返してきた。
examples.en: On my way out to go shopping, I returned the books I had borrowed to the library.
examples.f: ｜買い物[かいもの]に｜行[い]きがてら、｜借[か]りていた｜本[ほん]を｜図書館[としょかん]に｜返[かえ]してきた。

synonyms.note: かたがた joins two purposes in stiff, formal register and only attaches to nouns; がてら is casual and often centres on a trip.
ついでに treats the second act as an incidental afterthought; がてら presents both as roughly planned into the one outing.

related.note: かたわら pairs two long-term pursuits; がてら pairs two acts squeezed into a single occasion.

entry.title: 〜かたわら
entry.meaning: while; alongside (one's main occupation or activity)
entry.summary: 〜かたわら presents two ongoing pursuits: while doing A as one's main occupation, one also does B on the side over the same period. 傍ら literally means 'beside', and the figure is of B running parallel to a central activity — 仕事のかたわら (alongside one's work), 教えるかたわら (while teaching). It attaches to a dictionary-form verb or a noun + の, and belongs to written, somewhat literary style.
pitfalls: Describes two activities sustained over a long period (a main one plus a side one), not two acts done on a single occasion.
The clause before かたわら names the main occupation; the side activity comes after.
Written and literary; heavier than everyday 〜ながら.

examples.ja: 彼は大学で経済学を教えるかたわら、小説を書き続けている。
examples.en: Alongside teaching economics at the university, he continues to write novels.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]は｜大学[だいがく]で｜経済[けいざい]｜学[がく]を｜教[おし]えるかたわら、｜小説[しょうせつ]を｜書[か]き｜続[つづ]けている。

examples.ja: 家業を手伝うかたわら、地域のボランティア活動にも力を注いできた。
examples.en: While helping with the family business, she has also devoted her energy to local volunteer work.
examples.f: ｜家業[かぎょう]を｜手伝[てつだ]うかたわら、｜地域[ちいき]のボランティア｜活動[かつどう]にも｜力[ちから]を｜注[そそ]いできた。

synonyms.note: ながら links two actions happening at the same moment; かたわら links two ongoing pursuits carried on over a long stretch of one's life.

related.note: かたがた joins two purposes within one single act; かたわら sets one long-term side activity beside a main occupation.

entry.title: 〜が早いか
entry.meaning: no sooner than; the instant that
entry.summary: 〜が早いか says that the moment A happened, B followed almost simultaneously — 'no sooner had A than B'. It attaches to a dictionary-form (occasionally た-form) verb and belongs to written, narrative style. The second event is typically a sudden, vigorous action that actually took place, so the whole describes a real past sequence with the two events nearly overlapping in time.
pitfalls: The second event follows almost instantly — the two are essentially simultaneous, not merely 'soon after'.
B describes something that really happened (past), not a command, intention, or negative.
Literary and written; unnatural in casual conversation.

examples.ja: 終業のベルが鳴るが早いか、生徒たちは教室を飛び出していった。
examples.en: No sooner had the closing bell rung than the students dashed out of the classroom.
examples.f: ｜終業[しゅうぎょう]のベルが｜鳴[な]るが｜早[はや]いか、｜生徒[せいと]たちは｜教室[きょうしつ]を｜飛び出[とびだ]していった。

examples.ja: その知らせを聞くが早いか、彼は席を立って部屋を出て行った。
examples.en: The instant he heard the news, he rose from his seat and left the room.
examples.f: その｜知[し]らせを｜聞[き]くが｜早[はや]いか、｜彼[かれ]は｜席[せき]を｜立[た]って｜部屋[へや]を｜出[で]て｜行[い]った。

synonyms.note: や否や is nearly identical and equally literary; が早いか leans a touch more toward a briskly following, deliberate action.
なり also marks an immediate next action, often one the speaker found unexpected; が早いか stresses the near-simultaneity of the timing.

related.note: たとたん often marks a sudden change or realization at that moment; が早いか highlights a swift follow-on action in narration.

entry.title: 〜すら・〜ですら
entry.meaning: even; even so much as (emphatic)
entry.summary: すら singles out an extreme example to imply that if even this holds, the rest goes without saying — 専門家ですら分からない = even experts don't understand (so of course others don't). It attaches to a noun (ですら adds a copula-like emphasis) and very often pairs with a negative predicate. It is the more formal, literary counterpart of さえ.
pitfalls: すら is more formal and literary than さえ; in casual speech さえ is the natural choice.
It typically presents an extreme case and is very often followed by a negative.

examples.ja: 忙しすぎて、昼食をとる時間すらない。
examples.en: I'm so busy I don't even have time to eat lunch.
examples.f: ｜忙[いそが]しすぎて、｜昼食[ちゅうしょく]をとる｜時間[じかん]すらない。

examples.ja: その理論は、専門家ですら完全には説明できないという。
examples.en: They say that even specialists cannot fully explain that theory.
examples.f: その｜理論[りろん]は、｜専門[せんもん]｜家[か]ですら｜完全[かんぜん]には｜説明[せつめい]できないという。

synonyms.note: さえ carries the same 'even' emphasis but is more neutral and everyday; すら is more literary.
だに also means 'even', but is archaic and limited to set phrases; すら is freer to use.

entry.title: 〜ずくめ
entry.meaning: nothing but; entirely; full of
entry.summary: Noun＋ずくめ means the whole of something consists of that noun through and through: いいことずくめ = nothing but good things, 黒ずくめ = (dressed) all in black, 規則ずくめ = rules upon rules. It attaches to a limited group of nouns — colors, ごちそう, いいこと, 規則, 異例 — and, unlike だらけ, it happily describes good things as well as oppressive ones. It often characterizes a period, an outfit, or an organization.
pitfalls: Only a conventional set of nouns takes ずくめ (黒, いいこと, ごちそう, 規則, 異例...); you cannot coin freely with it.
It is not inherently negative — いいことずくめ is common; for 'covered in something undesirable', だらけ is the right choice.
Standard orthography is ずくめ, not づくめ.

examples.ja: 今年は結婚に昇進にと、いいことずくめの一年だった。
examples.en: With a wedding and a promotion, this was a year full of nothing but good things.
examples.f: ｜今年[ことし]は｜結婚[けっこん]に｜昇進[しょうしん]にと、いいことずくめの｜一[いち]｜年[ねん]だった。

examples.ja: 黒ずくめの服装の男が、店の前にじっと立っていた。
examples.en: A man dressed entirely in black was standing motionless in front of the shop.
examples.f: ｜黒[くろ]ずくめの｜服装[ふくそう]の｜男[おとこ]が、｜店[みせ]の｜前[まえ]にじっと｜立[た]っていた。

synonyms.note: だらけ means 'full of / covered in' something undesirable (泥だらけ, 間違いだらけ); ずくめ can be entirely positive.
まみれ is physical smearing over a surface (汗まみれ); ずくめ says the whole content or makeup is that thing.

entry.title: 〜てからというもの
entry.meaning: ever since ~; from the time ~, and continuing ever after
entry.summary: 〜てからというもの marks a past event as the turning point after which a state has held continuously ever since. 引っ越してからというもの、一度も会っていない = ever since I moved, I haven't seen them even once. It is more emphatic and emotive than plain てから, stressing that a lasting change set in from that moment and persists. The following clause describes the ongoing situation.
structure: Verb［て form］＋からというもの
pitfalls: Points to a lasting change that has continued ever since a single past event, not a one-time result.
More emphatic and emotional than plain 〜てから; reserve it for a genuine before-and-after shift.

examples.ja: あの本に出会ってからというもの、彼の人生観は大きく変わった。
examples.en: Ever since he came across that book, his outlook on life changed completely.
examples.f: あの｜本[ほん]に｜出会[であ]ってからというもの、｜彼[かれ]の｜人生[じんせい]｜観[かん]は｜大[おお]きく｜変[か]わった。

examples.ja: 犬を飼い始めてからというもの、毎朝の散歩が日課になった。
examples.en: Ever since we started keeping a dog, a walk every morning has become part of the routine.
examples.f: ｜犬[いぬ]を｜飼[か]い｜始[はじ]めてからというもの、｜毎朝[まいあさ]の｜散歩[さんぽ]が｜日課[にっか]になった。

synonyms.note: 〜て以来 also means 'ever since ~' and is more neutral and objective; てからというもの adds emotional emphasis on the sustained change.

related.note: plain 〜てから just orders one action after another; てからというもの stresses a lasting change that has held ever since.

entry.title: 〜てやまない
entry.meaning: to never cease to (wish, hope, love); to ~ from the bottom of one's heart
entry.summary: 〜てやまない attaches to the て-form of a verb of emotion or desire and says the speaker holds that feeling ceaselessly, straight from the heart. It pairs only with a small set of feeling verbs — 願う, 祈る, 期待する, 愛する, 尊敬する — so 願ってやまない = never cease to wish, 尊敬してやまない = hold in unending respect. It is formal, literary language at home in speeches, tributes, and written prose.
pitfalls: Only a small set of emotion/desire verbs fit: 願う, 祈る, 期待する, 愛する, 尊敬する. It does not attach to ordinary action verbs (×食べてやまない).
Formal, written or ceremonial language; it sounds out of place in casual conversation.

examples.ja: 皆様の今後ますますのご活躍を願ってやみません。
examples.en: I wish you all continued and ever-greater success in the days ahead.
examples.f: ｜皆様[みなさま]の｜今後[こんご]ますますのご｜活躍[かつやく]を｜願[ねが]ってやみません。

examples.ja: 彼は生涯、故郷の海と山を愛してやまなかった。
examples.en: All his life, he never ceased to love the sea and mountains of his hometown.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]は｜生涯[しょうがい]、｜故郷[こきょう]の｜海[うみ]と｜山[やま]を｜愛[あい]してやまなかった。

synonyms.note: てたまらない voices an emotion the speaker can hardly bear right now; てやまない is a lasting, heartfelt wish or feeling in formal prose.

related.note: てならない marks a feeling that wells up spontaneously and won't be suppressed; てやまない stresses a devoted feeling held without end.

entry.title: 〜と相まって
entry.meaning: combined with; coupled with; in tandem with
entry.summary: 〜と相まって marks that one factor works together with another to produce a heightened result — 'combined with ~, coupled with ~'. A が B と相まって means A, together with B, brings something about, and the two factors reinforce each other so the outcome is notably strong. It is formal, written-style language, common in commentary and description.
pitfalls: The two factors combine to strengthen a single outcome; it is not a plain 'A and B' listing.
Formal written style; 相まって is the て-form of 相まつ and is rarely heard in casual talk.

examples.ja: 彼の才能は、たゆまぬ努力と相まって、見事な結果を生んだ。
examples.en: His talent, coupled with tireless effort, produced splendid results.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]の｜才能[さいのう]は、たゆまぬ｜努力[どりょく]と｜相[あい]まって、｜見事[みごと]な｜結果[けっか]を｜生[う]んだ。

examples.ja: 円安が原油高と相まって、物価は急激に上昇した。
examples.en: The weak yen, combined with high crude-oil prices, drove prices up sharply.
examples.f: ｜円[えん]｜安[やす]が｜原油[げんゆ]｜高[だか]と｜相[あい]まって、｜物価[ぶっか]は｜急激[きゅうげき]に｜上昇[じょうしょう]した。

related.note: だけに gives a single reason all the more fitting for its nature; と相まって says two factors act together to amplify a result.

entry.title: 〜ならでは
entry.meaning: unique to; only possible for; distinctive of
entry.summary: 〜ならでは(の) praises something as achievable only by the named person, place, or thing: その店ならではの味 = a flavor only that shop can produce. It usually appears as ならではの + noun or ならではだ, and the tone is admiring — it credits a quality to the special character of the referent that nothing else could match.
pitfalls: It carries positive, appreciative force ('only ~ could pull this off'); it is not used to point out drawbacks.
The usual shape is ならではの followed by a noun; ならでは rarely stands without の or だ.

examples.ja: この祭りには、この土地ならではの活気がある。
examples.en: This festival has a liveliness you'll find only in this region.
examples.f: この｜祭[まつ]りには、この｜土地[とち]ならではの｜活気[かっき]がある。

examples.ja: 細部への気配りは、彼女ならではのものだ。
examples.en: This attention to the finest details is something only she can bring.
examples.f: ｜細部[さいぶ]への｜気配[きくば]りは、｜彼女[かのじょ]ならではのものだ。

related.note: だけあって explains an impressive result as living up to a background ('as you'd expect of ~'); ならでは credits a quality as uniquely possible for the referent.

entry.title: 〜べく
entry.meaning: in order to ~; so as to ~ (literary)
entry.summary: 〜べく expresses purpose in a formal, written register — 'in order to ~, so as to ~'. 目標を達成すべく = in order to achieve the goal. It follows a dictionary-form verb (する → すべく or するべく), and the main clause describes a deliberate action taken toward that aim. It is the literary cousin of ように and ために.
pitfalls: Formal and written; it does not appear in casual conversation.
With する, both すべく and するべく occur (すべく is more classical). The main clause should be a deliberate action taken for that purpose, not a spontaneous happening.

examples.ja: 新市場に参入すべく、会社は大規模な調査を開始した。
examples.en: In order to enter the new market, the company launched a large-scale survey.
examples.f: ｜新[しん]｜市場[しじょう]に｜参入[さんにゅう]すべく、｜会社[かいしゃ]は｜大[だい]｜規模[きぼ]な｜調査[ちょうさ]を｜開始[かいし]した。

examples.ja: 事故の原因を究明すべく、専門家チームが結成された。
examples.en: A team of experts was formed in order to determine the cause of the accident.
examples.f: ｜事故[じこ]の｜原因[げんいん]を｜究明[きゅうめい]すべく、｜専門[せんもん]｜家[か]チームが｜結成[けっせい]された。

synonyms.note: ために is the everyday 'in order to'; べく expresses the same purpose in a literary register.

related.note: べくして (as was bound to happen) uses the same べく root but expresses inevitability, not purpose.

entry.title: 〜ようものなら
entry.meaning: if one were to (even slightly) do ~, dire consequences would follow
entry.summary: 〜ようものなら takes a volitional-form verb and warns that if that action were so much as attempted, something serious or disastrous would happen. The consequence is heavy and often exaggerated: 少しでも文句を言おうものなら大変なことになる = if you dared to complain even a little, all hell would break loose. It expresses the speaker's sense that the situation is so touchy that the smallest move triggers an outsized reaction.
pitfalls: Distinguish the two ものなら: with the volitional (言おうものなら) it means 'if one were to, with dire results'; with the potential (できるものなら) it means 'if one could'.
The result clause is negative and often hyperbolic — the point is how extreme the reaction to a small act would be.

examples.ja: 彼の前でその話題に触れようものなら、何時間も説教が続くだろう。
examples.en: If you so much as brought up that topic in front of him, the lecture would go on for hours.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]の｜前[まえ]でその｜話題[わだい]に｜触[ふ]れようものなら、｜何[なん]｜時間[じかん]も｜説教[せっきょう]が｜続[つづ]くだろう。

examples.ja: 少しでも手を抜こうものなら、監督にすぐ見抜かれてしまう。
examples.en: If you were to cut corners even a little, the coach would see through it in no time.
examples.f: ｜少[すこ]しでも｜手[て]を｜抜[ぬ]こうものなら、｜監督[かんとく]にすぐ｜見抜[みぬ]かれてしまう。

synonyms.note: The potential-based ものなら (できるものなら) expresses a wish 'if only one could'; ようものなら uses the volitional to warn of dire results.

entry.title: 〜を禁じ得ない
entry.meaning: cannot suppress (an emotion); can't help feeling
entry.summary: 〜を禁じ得ない takes an emotion noun and says one cannot forbid it welling up: 涙を禁じ得ない = can't hold back tears; 怒りを禁じ得ない = can't suppress anger. 禁じ得ない literally means 'cannot forbid (in oneself)'. It is distinctly formal, appearing in written and formal-spoken contexts, and describes a feeling that arises naturally in the speaker or as a general human reaction.
pitfalls: The object is an emotion noun (涙・怒り・驚き・同情), not an action — you can't say 行くのを禁じ得ない.
Formal register; describes an emotion welling up in oneself, so it isn't used to report someone else's feelings casually.

examples.ja: あまりに理不尽な仕打ちに、怒りを禁じ得なかった。
examples.en: Faced with such an unreasonable act, I could not suppress my anger.
examples.f: あまりに｜理不尽[りふじん]な｜仕打[しう]ちに、｜怒[いか]りを｜禁[きん]じ｜得[え]なかった。

examples.ja: 被災地の惨状を目にして、涙を禁じ得なかった。
examples.en: Seeing the devastation in the disaster area, I could not hold back my tears.
examples.f: ｜被災[ひさい]｜地[ち]の｜惨状[さんじょう]を｜目[め]にして、｜涙[なみだ]を｜禁[きん]じ｜得[え]なかった。

synonyms.note: ざるを得ない = have no choice but to (do an action); を禁じ得ない = cannot suppress (an emotion) — different objects.

related.note: 〜に堪えない (感慨に堪えない) also expresses an overwhelming feeling; を禁じ得ない specifically frames it as an emotion one cannot hold back.

entry.title: 〜を余儀なくされる
entry.meaning: to be forced to; to have no choice but to (undergo)
entry.summary: 〜を余儀なくされる is the passive side of the pair: the person or organization affected is the subject, and outside circumstances leave them no choice but to accept some outcome. The unwanted outcome is an action noun (欠場, 閉鎖, 延期) marked with を. けがで欠場を余儀なくされた = was forced to sit out because of injury. It stresses that the situation was imposed from without, and it belongs to formal, written register.
pitfalls: The affected person is the subject and the を-noun is what they are forced into; contrast 〜を余儀なくさせる, where the cause is the subject.
The を-noun is normally a する-type action noun such as 中止・閉鎖・延期.
It emphasizes that circumstances imposed the outcome, so it carries a sense of reluctance and belongs to formal writing.

examples.ja: 出場予定だった選手は、けがのために欠場を余儀なくされた。
examples.en: The player who had been slated to compete was forced to withdraw because of an injury.
examples.f: ｜出場[しゅつじょう]｜予定[よてい]だった｜選手[せんしゅ]は、けがのために｜欠場[けつじょう]を｜余儀[よぎ]なくされた。

examples.ja: 業績の悪化により、会社は多くの店舗の閉鎖を余儀なくされた。
examples.en: With performance deteriorating, the company had no choice but to close many of its stores.
examples.f: ｜業績[ぎょうせき]の｜悪化[あっか]により、｜会社[かいしゃ]は｜多[おお]くの｜店舗[てんぽ]の｜閉鎖[へいさ]を｜余儀[よぎ]なくされた。

synonyms.note: ざるを得ない attaches to a verb and voices personal, reluctant resignation; を余儀なくされる attaches to an action noun and stresses that external circumstances imposed it.
しかない plainly says 'there is nothing to do but'; を余儀なくされる is far more formal and frames the outcome as forced upon one from outside.

related.note: The causative counterpart: 〜を余儀なくさせる makes the cause the subject, while 〜を余儀なくされる makes the forced person the subject.

entry.title: 〜あっての
entry.meaning: which exists only thanks to; made possible only by
entry.summary: 〜あっての joins two nouns: 'A あっての B' means B exists or holds true only because A is there — take A away and B collapses. 客あっての商売 = a business is nothing without its customers, 健康あっての仕事 = work only matters if you have your health. It stresses that the first noun is the indispensable foundation for the second. The pattern is emphatic and set in feel.
structure: Noun［essential thing］＋あっての＋Noun［what depends on it］
pitfalls: Order matters: 'A あっての B' means B depends on A, not the other way round.
Both slots are nouns and あっての links them directly — no の or な in between.

examples.ja: 読者あっての雑誌なのだから、読者の声を第一に考えるべきだ。
examples.en: A magazine is nothing without its readers, so their voices should come first.
examples.f: ｜読者[どくしゃ]あっての｜雑誌[ざっし]なのだから、｜読者[どくしゃ]の｜声[こえ]を｜第[だい]｜一[いち]に｜考[かんが]えるべきだ。

examples.ja: 日々の努力あっての結果であり、決して偶然ではない。
examples.en: This result came about only through daily effort; it was by no means luck.
examples.f: ｜日々[ひび]の｜努力[どりょく]あっての｜結果[けっか]であり、｜決[けっ]して｜偶然[ぐうぜん]ではない。

synonyms.note: 〜てこそ also says something holds true 'only through / precisely because of', but attaches to a verb clause; あっての links two nouns.

entry.title: 〜ようが・〜ようと
entry.meaning: no matter what/how; even if; regardless of ~
entry.summary: A single volitional followed by が or と means 'no matter ~ / even if ~': 何を言われようが = no matter what I'm told, どうなろうと = no matter what happens. It concedes any possibility and states that the main clause holds all the same. With adjectives it uses かろう (どんなに苦しかろうと), and with nouns/な-adjectives であろう (誰であろうと). It is emphatic and more formal than ても.
pitfalls: が and と are interchangeable here; both mean 'no matter ~'.
It is emphatic and somewhat formal; plain ても is the more everyday 'even if'.

examples.ja: 周りに何と言われようと、私はこの道を進むと決めている。
examples.en: No matter what people around me say, I've decided to go down this path.
examples.f: ｜周[まわ]りに｜何[なに]と｜言[い]われようと、｜私[わたし]はこの｜道[みち]を｜進[すす]むと｜決[き]めている。

examples.ja: どんなに困難な状況になろうと、最後まで諦めるつもりはない。
examples.en: No matter how difficult the situation becomes, I have no intention of giving up until the very end.
examples.f: どんなに｜困難[こんなん]な｜状況[じょうきょう]になろうと、｜最後[さいご]まで｜諦[あきら]めるつもりはない。

synonyms.note: ても is the everyday 'even if ~'; 〜ようと／ようが is more emphatic and formal, stressing 'no matter what'.
doubling it (ようが〜ようが) lists two specific alternatives; the single form concedes any possibility at all.

related.note: もかまわず means 'without regard for ~ (and acting anyway)'; 〜ようと states that the outcome holds no matter the case.

entry.title: 〜限りだ
entry.meaning: feel utterly ~; extremely (of an emotion)
entry.summary: 〜限りだ, after an emotion word, expresses that the speaker feels that emotion to the utmost — 'I couldn't be more ~'. 嬉しい限りだ = I couldn't be happier; 心細い限りだ = I feel utterly forlorn; 羨ましい限りだ = I'm terribly envious. It takes an い-adjective, or a な-adjective + な, of feeling and states the speaker's own emotion at its extreme. The tone is somewhat formal.
pitfalls: 限りだ attaches to emotion words and describes the speaker's own feeling at its peak; it isn't used for others' emotions or for non-emotional degrees.

examples.ja: 旧友が遠くから駆けつけてくれて、心強い限りだ。
examples.en: With an old friend rushing over from afar to help, I couldn't feel more reassured.
examples.f: ｜旧友[きゅうゆう]が｜遠[とお]くから｜駆[か]けつけてくれて、｜心強[こころづよ]い｜限[かぎ]りだ。

examples.ja: 長年の研究がこうして実を結び、嬉しい限りです。
examples.en: To see many years of research bear fruit like this, I couldn't be happier.
examples.f: ｜長年[ながねん]の｜研究[けんきゅう]がこうして｜実[み]を｜結[むす]び、｜嬉[うれ]しい｜限[かぎ]りです。

synonyms.note: 〜の至り expresses reaching the height of a feeling (formal, set phrases like 光栄の至り); 限りだ is a slightly less rigid 'utterly ~'.
〜の極み marks the extreme peak of a state (感激の極み); 限りだ centers the speaker's own emotion 'to the utmost'.

related.note: 〜極まりない says a quality is 'extreme beyond limit' (often negative); 限りだ voices a personal emotion at its height.

entry.title: 〜かたがた
entry.meaning: while also; combining the purpose of; partly in order to
entry.summary: 〜かたがた marks that a single action serves two purposes at once — the main one, plus the かたがた one done along with it. It attaches to a noun, almost always a formal social act such as 挨拶かたがた (partly to pay one's respects), お礼かたがた (partly to say thanks), or お詫びかたがた (partly to apologize). The tone is stiff and old-fashioned, at home in letters and polite visits. One deed accomplishes both aims.
pitfalls: Attaches to a noun (usually a formal suru-noun like 挨拶・お礼・お詫び), not to a verb.
One single action fulfils both purposes at the same time; it is not two separate errands.
Formal and written; in casual speech がてら or ついでに are more natural.

examples.ja: 先日のお礼かたがた、近くまで参りましたのでお立ち寄りいたしました。
examples.en: Partly to thank you for the other day, and since I happened to be in the area, I have dropped by.
examples.f: ｜先日[せんじつ]のお｜礼[れい]かたがた、｜近[ちか]くまで｜参[まい]りましたのでお｜立ち寄[たちよ]りいたしました。

examples.ja: 帰省かたがた、長らくご無沙汰していた恩師のお宅を訪ねた。
examples.en: On my trip back to my hometown, I also visited the home of the mentor I had long neglected to contact.
examples.f: ｜帰省[きせい]かたがた、｜長[なが]らくご｜無沙汰[ぶさた]していた｜恩師[おんし]のお｜宅[たく]を｜訪[たず]ねた。

synonyms.note: がてら does two things on one outing too, but is more casual and often involves physically going somewhere; かたがた is formal and noun-only.

related.note: ついでに frames the second action as an afterthought taken while doing the first; かたがた presents both purposes as intended together, in stiffer register.
かたわら pairs two sustained activities over a long span; かたがた joins two purposes in one single act.

entry.title: 〜かと思いきや
entry.meaning: contrary to what one thought; one would think ~, but actually
entry.summary: 〜かと思いきや sets up an expectation and then overturns it: you thought A, but in fact the opposite or something quite different turned out to be the case. 思いきや is a fixed classical form and gives the phrase a slightly literary, sometimes wry tone. It attaches to a plain-form clause (a noun or な-adjective may drop だ). The reality after it always contradicts the assumption before it.
pitfalls: What follows always reverses the expectation — never merely continues or confirms it.
思いきや is a frozen classical form; it is not conjugated further.
Literary and often lightly humorous; not for neutral, matter-of-fact writing.

examples.ja: 作業は簡単に終わるかと思いきや、予想外の問題が次々と出てきた。
examples.en: I thought the work would finish easily, but contrary to expectation one unforeseen problem after another cropped up.
examples.f: ｜作業[さぎょう]は｜簡単[かんたん]に｜終[お]わるかと｜思[おも]いきや、｜予想[よそう]｜外[がい]の｜問題[もんだい]が｜次々[つぎつぎ]と｜出[で]てきた。

examples.ja: 桜はもう散ってしまったかと思いきや、日陰にはまだ花が残っていた。
examples.en: I assumed the cherry blossoms had already fallen, but to my surprise some flowers still lingered in the shade.
examples.f: ｜桜[さくら]はもう｜散[ち]ってしまったかと｜思[おも]いきや、｜日陰[ひかげ]にはまだ｜花[はな]が｜残[のこ]っていた。

related.note: に反して neutrally states a result running counter to an expectation or standard; かと思いきや dramatizes the speaker's own assumption being upended.
とはいえ concedes a point then qualifies it; かと思いきや reveals that the anticipated situation was simply wrong.

entry.title: 〜嫌いがある
entry.meaning: to have a (bad) tendency to; to be inclined to
entry.summary: 〜嫌いがある points out an unfavourable disposition — a tendency to do something the speaker regards as regrettable. 物事を悲観的に考える嫌いがある = to have a tendency to think about things pessimistically. It attaches to a dictionary- or ない-form verb, or a noun + の, and belongs to formal, written style. The 嫌い here means 'inclination', unrelated to the everyday word for 'dislike'.
structure: Verb［dictionary form／ない form］＋嫌いがある
pitfalls: Describes a negative predisposition and carries mild criticism; not used for good tendencies.
嫌い here means 'inclination', not 'dislike' — don't read it as the emotion.
Formal and written; heavier and more judgmental than casual がち.

examples.ja: 彼はどうも物事を大げさに考える嫌いがある。
examples.en: He does seem to have a tendency to think about things in an exaggerated way.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]はどうも｜物事[ものごと]を｜大[おお]げさに｜考[かんが]える｜嫌[きら]いがある。

examples.ja: 最近の報道は、物事の一面だけを強調する嫌いがあるように思う。
examples.en: Recent news coverage seems to have a tendency to emphasize only one side of things.
examples.f: ｜最近[さいきん]の｜報道[ほうどう]は、｜物事[ものごと]の｜一[いち]｜面[めん]だけを｜強調[きょうちょう]する｜嫌[きら]いがあるように｜思[おも]う。

synonyms.note: がち is casual and simply notes a frequent tendency; 嫌いがある is formal and pointedly critical of an ingrained inclination.

entry.title: 〜の極み
entry.meaning: the extreme of; the height of; the epitome of
entry.summary: 〜の極み marks a state pushed to its absolute limit — 贅沢の極み = the height of luxury, 疲労の極み = utter exhaustion, 混乱の極み = total chaos. It attaches to a noun naming a condition and says that condition has reached its furthest point. This is formal, written or dramatic Japanese, used for both positive and negative extremes.
pitfalls: It attaches to nouns naming a state or condition (贅沢・混乱・疲労・感激) and pushes it to its limit.
の至り is largely confined to emotions in humble set phrases; の極み ranges more widely, over states good and bad.

examples.ja: 毎晩高級店で食事をするとは、贅沢の極みだ。
examples.en: Dining at high-end restaurants every night is the height of extravagance.
examples.f: ｜毎晩[まいばん]｜高級[こうきゅう]｜店[てん]で｜食事[しょくじ]をするとは、｜贅沢[ぜいたく]の｜極[きわ]みだ。

examples.ja: 準備不足のまま本番を迎え、会場は混乱の極みに達した。
examples.en: Going into the main event underprepared, the venue descended into utter chaos.
examples.f: ｜準備[じゅんび]｜不足[ふそく]のまま｜本番[ほんばん]を｜迎[むか]え、｜会場[かいじょう]は｜混乱[こんらん]の｜極[きわ]みに｜達[たっ]した。

synonyms.note: の至り is limited to peak emotions in humble set phrases; の極み covers a wider range of states, positive or negative.
この上ない means 'nothing surpasses it, the utmost'; の極み names the extreme point of a specific state as a noun.

entry.title: 〜こととて
entry.meaning: because; as (formal, often apologetic)
entry.summary: 〜こととて presents a circumstance as the reason for something — most often as an excuse when apologizing or asking for indulgence: 慣れぬこととて = as (I am) unaccustomed to it. It is markedly old-fashioned and formal, at home in business letters, formal apologies, and period fiction. It follows a plain-form clause or Noun＋の, and famously combines with the classical negative ぬ (知らぬこととて, 慣れぬこととて).
pitfalls: It is archaic-formal; using it in casual conversation sounds theatrical. In speech, ものですから or ので fills the same role.
With negatives it characteristically takes the classical ぬ (慣れぬこととて); the plain ない (慣れないこととて) is also used but sounds less set.
The main clause is usually an apology or a request for understanding, not a neutral consequence.

examples.ja: 何分新人のこととて、行き届かない点はどうかお許しください。
examples.en: As he is still new to the job, please forgive any points where he falls short.
examples.f: ｜何分[なにぶん]｜新人[しんじん]のこととて、｜行き届[いきとど]かない｜点[てん]はどうかお｜許[ゆる]しください。

examples.ja: 慣れぬこととて、ご迷惑をおかけしましたことを深くお詫び申し上げます。
examples.en: Being unaccustomed to the task, I sincerely apologize for the trouble I caused.
examples.f: ｜慣[な]れぬこととて、ご｜迷惑[めいわく]をおかけしましたことを｜深[ふか]くお｜詫[わ]び｜申し上[もうしあ]げます。

synonyms.note: もので also gives an excuse-flavored reason, but is ordinary polite speech; こととて is archaic and ceremonious.

related.note: ことだし casually offers one reason for a proposal; こととて formally excuses a shortcoming.

entry.title: 〜ことなしに
entry.meaning: without doing; unless (one does)
entry.summary: 〜ことなしに attaches to a dictionary-form verb and means the main action happens without that verb ever occurring: 誰にも相談することなしに決めた = decided without consulting anyone. In its second, more argumentative use, the main clause is negative or potential-negative and the whole sentence reads 'unless you do X, Y is impossible' — 努力することなしに成功はあり得ない. Both uses are formal and written in flavor; everyday speech would use 〜ないで or 〜ずに.
pitfalls: Attach it to the dictionary form via こと: 相談することなしに, not 相談したことなしに.
It is distinctly formal; for everyday 'without doing', 〜ないで or 〜ずに is the natural choice.
In the 'unless' use, the main clause must be negative in sense: 犠牲を払うことなしに自由は得られない.

examples.ja: 彼は誰にも相談することなしに、退職を決めてしまった。
examples.en: He decided to quit his job without consulting anyone at all.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]は｜誰[だれ]にも｜相談[そうだん]することなしに、｜退職[たいしょく]を｜決[き]めてしまった。

examples.ja: 地道に努力することなしに、成功はあり得ない。
examples.en: Success is impossible without steady, patient effort.
