examples.f: ｜地道[じみち]に｜努力[どりょく]することなしに、｜成功[せいこう]はあり｜得[え]ない。

synonyms.note: なしに attaches directly to nouns (連絡なしに); ことなしに packages a verb phrase into the same construction.
ないで is the neutral spoken 'without doing'; ことなしに is its stiff written counterpart.

related.note: なくしては ('without ~, no ...') also builds an 'impossible without' argument, but from a noun.

entry.title: 〜始末だ
entry.meaning: ended up (in a deplorable state); to top it all off
entry.summary: 〜始末だ caps off a chain of bad developments with the final, worst stage: 遅刻を繰り返し、ついには無断欠勤までする始末だ = he kept coming late, and to top it all off he started skipping work without notice. The speaker is exasperated or critical; the pattern almost demands set-up phrases like さんざん〜したあげく or ついには. It follows the dictionary form, and この始末だ ('look how it ended up') is a common set phrase.
pitfalls: The outcome must be deplorable and the speaker critical — it cannot report a happy ending: ×合格する始末だ.
It marks the last stage of a downhill sequence, so it usually needs lead-up like ついには or 〜たあげく.
Attach it to the dictionary form: 泣き出す始末だ, not 泣き出した始末だ.

examples.ja: 彼は遅刻を繰り返し、ついには無断欠勤までする始末だ。
examples.en: He kept showing up late, and to top it all off he even started skipping work without notice.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]は｜遅刻[ちこく]を｜繰り返[くりかえ]し、ついには｜無断[むだん]｜欠勤[けっきん]までする｜始末[しまつ]だ。

examples.ja: 兄はさんざん散財したあげく、友人にまでお金を借りる始末だった。
examples.en: After spending recklessly, my brother ended up borrowing money even from his friends.
examples.f: ｜兄[あに]はさんざん｜散財[さんざい]したあげく、｜友人[ゆうじん]にまでお｜金[かね]を｜借[か]りる｜始末[しまつ]だった。

synonyms.note: あげく marks 'after a long, trying process'; 始末だ goes further and condemns the final state it led to.

related.note: 末に is neutral about the outcome of a long process; 始末だ is reserved for outcomes the speaker deplores.
羽目になる laments the unlucky situation one falls into; 始末だ criticizes conduct that spiraled to a sorry end.

entry.title: 〜ずじまい
entry.meaning: ended up never doing (and the chance is gone)
entry.summary: 〜ずじまい combines the negative ず with 仕舞い ('the end') to say a period closed with the action never done — and the speaker regrets it: 結局行かずじまいだった = in the end I never did go. The chance is understood to be lost now. It follows the ない-stem (する becomes せずじまい), almost always appears in the past (〜ずじまいだった), and pairs naturally with 結局 or とうとう.
structure: Verb［ない stem］＋ずじまい（だった）
pitfalls: する becomes せずじまい — ×しずじまい is wrong.
It implies the opportunity has closed and carries regret; for a neutral 'didn't do', plain しなかった is enough.
It normally reports a finished period, so the past 〜ずじまいだった is the usual form.

examples.ja: 京都に三年も住んでいたのに、結局金閣寺には行かずじまいだった。
examples.en: Even though I lived in Kyoto for three whole years, I ended up never visiting Kinkaku-ji.
examples.f: ｜京都[きょうと]に｜三[さん]｜年[ねん]も｜住[す]んでいたのに、｜結局[けっきょく]｜金閣寺[きんかくじ]には｜行[い]かずじまいだった。

examples.ja: 言おう言おうと思いながら、本当の気持ちは伝えられずじまいだった。
examples.en: I kept meaning to say it, but in the end I never managed to convey my true feelings.
examples.f: ｜言[い]おう｜言[い]おうと｜思[おも]いながら、｜本当[ほんとう]の｜気持[きも]ちは｜伝[つた]えられずじまいだった。

related.note: 〜そこなう marks missing a particular chance to do something; ずじまい looks back on a whole period that ended without it.
ずとも is a concessive 'even without doing'; ずじまい reports that the doing never happened, with regret.

entry.title: 〜ずにはおかない・〜ないではおかない
entry.kana: ずにはおかない・ないではおかない
entry.romaji: zu niwa okanai / nai dewa okanai
entry.meaning: will inevitably cause; will not rest until
entry.summary: 〜ずにはおかない declares that a force will not let things end without the verb happening. With causative or emotive verbs, the subject is often a thing whose power inevitably affects people: 聴く人を感動させずにはおかない = it cannot fail to move listeners. With a personal subject it voices fierce determination: 謝らせずにはおかない = I won't rest until I make him apologize. It is emphatic, formal, and written in flavor; する becomes せずにはおかない.
structure: Verb［ない stem］＋ずにはおかない
Verb［ない form］＋ではおかない
pitfalls: Don't confuse it with ずにはいられない, which is the speaker's own uncontrollable urge; ずにはおかない is an external force or resolve that will inevitably bring the action about.
In the 'inevitable effect' use the verb is typically causative (感動させる, 考えさせる) and the subject is often a work, event, or statement.
する becomes せずにはおかない.

examples.ja: 彼女の歌声は、聴く人を感動させずにはおかない。
examples.en: Her singing voice never fails to move those who hear it.
examples.f: ｜彼女[かのじょ]の｜歌声[うたごえ]は、｜聴[き]く｜人[ひと]を｜感動[かんどう]させずにはおかない。

examples.ja: 今回の不正は、世間の厳しい批判を招かずにはおかないだろう。
examples.en: This misconduct is bound to draw harsh public criticism.
examples.f: ｜今回[こんかい]の｜不正[ふせい]は、｜世間[せけん]の｜厳[きび]しい｜批判[ひはん]を｜招[まね]かずにはおかないだろう。

related.note: ずにはいられない is an internal urge you cannot suppress; ずにはおかない is an outcome the force of things will not fail to produce.
ずには済まない says circumstances oblige you to act; ずにはおかない says the action will inevitably be brought about.

entry.title: 〜そばから
entry.meaning: as soon as (and it is immediately undone again); no sooner than
entry.summary: 〜そばから describes a repeated frustration: no sooner do you do X than the result is immediately undone, over and over. 片付けるそばから散らかす = the moment I tidy up, it gets messy again. It attaches to the dictionary or た-form and, unlike a one-time 'as soon as', implies a habitual cycle where effort is constantly negated.
pitfalls: It implies a repeated, habitual cycle, not a single one-off event.
The nuance is usually frustration that one's effort is undone again and again.

examples.ja: 新しい単語は、覚えるそばから忘れてしまう。
examples.en: No sooner do I memorize new words than I forget them again.
examples.f: ｜新[あたら]しい｜単語[たんご]は、｜覚[おぼ]えるそばから｜忘[わす]れてしまう。

examples.ja: 子どもが片付けるそばから、また部屋を散らかす。
examples.en: The moment I tidy up, the kids mess the room again.
examples.f: ｜子[こ]どもが｜片付[かたづ]けるそばから、また｜部屋[へや]を｜散[ち]らかす。

synonyms.note: が早いか marks a single 'the instant one did X, Y happened'; そばから stresses a repeated, recurring pattern.
たとたん marks one sudden moment; そばから implies the undoing happens again and again.

entry.title: 〜たりとも
entry.meaning: not even a single ~; not so much as one ~
entry.summary: たりとも follows '一 + counter' and pairs with a negative to mean 'not even one' — 一日たりとも忘れない = I won't forget for even a single day, 一円たりとも無駄にできない = can't waste even one yen. It is emphatic and literary. The separate idiom 何人（なんぴと）たりとも means 'no one whosoever'.
pitfalls: It is fixed with 一 + a counter and requires a negative: it means 'not even one'.
何人（なんぴと）たりとも is a separate set idiom meaning 'no one whosoever', not the counting use.

examples.ja: この計画では、一日たりとも無駄にはできない。
examples.en: In this plan, we cannot afford to waste even a single day.
examples.f: この｜計画[けいかく]では、｜一[いち]｜日[にち]たりとも｜無駄[むだ]にはできない。

examples.ja: 敵を前に、兵士たちは一瞬たりとも気を緩めなかった。
examples.en: Facing the enemy, the soldiers did not let their guard down for even an instant.
examples.f: ｜敵[てき]を｜前[まえ]に、｜兵士[へいし]たちは｜一瞬[いっしゅん]たりとも｜気[き]を｜緩[ゆる]めなかった。

synonyms.note: も with a minimal amount and a negative also gives 'not even ~'; たりとも is more emphatic and literary, and locks onto 一 + counter.

related.note: だに also gives an emphatic 'not even', but attaches to nouns/verbs in set phrases; たりとも counts with 一 + a counter.

entry.title: 〜だに・〜だにしない
entry.meaning: even (just); (not) even
entry.summary: だに is an archaic 'even' surviving mainly in fixed expressions. With an affirmative, 想像するだに恐ろしい = it is terrifying just to imagine. In the form 〜だにしない it means 'not even ~': 微動だにしない = doesn't budge in the slightest, 予想だにしなかった = didn't even imagine. It attaches to a dictionary-form verb or noun and is strongly literary.
pitfalls: だに is archaic and not freely productive; it lives mostly in set phrases (想像するだに, 微動だにしない, 予想だにしない).
For a plain, modern 'even', use さえ or すら instead.

examples.ja: あんな悲劇が起こるとは、当時は予想だにしなかった。
examples.en: At the time, I never even imagined that such a tragedy could happen.
examples.f: あんな｜悲劇[ひげき]が｜起[お]こるとは、｜当時[とうじ]は｜予想[よそう]だにしなかった。

examples.ja: 厳しい批判を浴びても、彼の決意は微動だにしなかった。
examples.en: Even under harsh criticism, his resolve did not waver in the slightest.
examples.f: ｜厳[きび]しい｜批判[ひはん]を｜浴[あ]びても、｜彼[かれ]の｜決意[けつい]は｜微動[びどう]だにしなかった。

synonyms.note: すら is emphatic 'even' and freer to use; だに is archaic and confined to fixed expressions.
さえ is the everyday 'even'; だに is its literary, restricted counterpart.

entry.title: 〜つ〜つ
entry.meaning: now ~ now ~; alternately doing one thing and its opposite
entry.summary: A literary pattern that joins two verb stems (連用形) each with つ, describing two actions that alternate or play off one another — typically a pair of opposites. 行きつ戻りつ = pacing back and forth, 追いつ追われつ = chasing and being chased by turns. It survives mainly in set expressions, often pairing one active verb with its passive form. The tone is descriptive and literary, not everyday speech.
pitfalls: Mostly limited to fixed pairs (行きつ戻りつ, 浮きつ沈みつ, 追いつ追われつ); it is not freely productive with any two verbs.
The two verbs are usually opposites, and often one is the active and the other the passive form of the same verb.

examples.ja: 小舟が波に浮きつ沈みつしていた。
examples.en: The small boat bobbed on the waves, rising and sinking by turns.
examples.f: ｜小舟[こぶね]が｜波[なみ]に｜浮[う]きつ｜沈[しず]みつしていた。

examples.ja: 彼は返事を書こうとして、部屋を行きつ戻りつしていた。
examples.en: Trying to write a reply, he paced back and forth across the room.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]は｜返事[へんじ]を｜書[か]こうとして、｜部屋[へや]を｜行[い]きつ｜戻[もど]りつしていた。

synonyms.note: 〜たり〜たり is the everyday way to list alternating or representative actions; つ〜つ is a frozen literary form confined to set opposite-verb pairs.

related.note: つつ ('while / although') marks one action accompanying another and is fully productive; the doubled つ〜つ is a separate fixed pattern for two alternating actions.

entry.title: 〜てしかるべきだ
entry.meaning: ought to be ~; it is only natural/proper that ~; deserves to be ~
entry.summary: 〜てしかるべきだ says something is proper and to be expected — it ought to be so as a matter of course. 努力は評価されてしかるべきだ = such effort ought to be, and deserves to be, recognized. しかるべき means 'appropriate / as it should be', so the phrase asserts that the state described by the て-form is the natural, reasonable thing. It is formal and often argues that something rightly should happen.
pitfalls: Formal, written or argumentative register; not for everyday conversation.
It often attaches to a passive て-form (評価されて, 認められて) to say 'ought rightly to be ~ed'.

examples.ja: これだけの成果を上げたのだから、正当に評価されてしかるべきだ。
examples.en: Having produced results of this magnitude, he ought by rights to be properly recognized.
examples.f: これだけの｜成果[せいか]を｜上[あ]げたのだから、｜正当[せいとう]に｜評価[ひょうか]されてしかるべきだ。

examples.ja: 消費者への説明があってしかるべきだったが、企業は沈黙を続けた。
examples.en: There should by rights have been an explanation to consumers, yet the company kept silent.
examples.f: ｜消費[しょうひ]｜者[しゃ]への｜説明[せつめい]があってしかるべきだったが、｜企業[きぎょう]は｜沈黙[ちんもく]を｜続[つづ]けた。

synonyms.note: plain 〜べきだ states a direct 'should / ought to'; てしかるべきだ frames it as what is only natural and proper, often more measured and formal.
〜て当然だ ('naturally ~; no wonder ~') also says something is to be expected; てしかるべきだ adds the sense that it is the proper, deserved thing.

entry.title: 手前
entry.meaning: seeing as ~; given one's position before others
entry.summary: 手前 as a grammar pattern means 'because of one's standing or appearance in front of others, one has to ~'. Following a noun + の or a plain-form verb, it gives a reason rooted in pride, face, or obligation toward the people watching — 約束した手前 = 'having promised (and with others aware), I can't back out'. The following clause states what one must or cannot do to save face.
pitfalls: This 手前 gives a reason based on one's face or position before others; it is not the literal 手前 meaning 'in front of / this side'.
The main clause states an obligation or restraint one accepts to keep up appearances (can't refuse, can't complain).

examples.ja: 後輩たちの手前、弱音を吐くわけにはいかない。
examples.en: With my juniors watching, I can't let myself complain.
examples.f: ｜後輩[こうはい]たちの｜手前[てまえ]、｜弱音[よわね]を｜吐[は]くわけにはいかない。

examples.ja: 一度引き受けると言った手前、今さら断れない。
examples.en: Having said I'd take it on, I can't very well refuse now.
examples.f: ｜一度[いちど]｜引き受[ひきう]けると｜言[い]った｜手前[てまえ]、｜今[いま]さら｜断[ことわ]れない。

synonyms.note: 以上は gives a logical 'now that ~, naturally ~'; 手前 grounds the obligation specifically in appearances before others.
からには means 'now that / so long as ~', stressing resolve; 手前 stresses saving face in front of people.

related.note: 上は means 'now that ~ (I've done it), I must ~'; 手前 adds the specific motive of pride or appearances.

entry.title: 〜とあって
entry.meaning: because (of the special circumstance); given that
entry.summary: 〜とあって presents a special or noteworthy circumstance as the reason a fitting consequence follows naturally — 'because it's ~, given that ~'. 連休とあって = it being a long holiday (so naturally...), 人気店とあって = as it's a popular shop. The situation is unusual or newsworthy enough that the result comes as a matter of course. It is common in reportage and in describing others' situations objectively.
pitfalls: The reason is a special or notable situation and the result follows naturally; it is not used for ordinary, everyday causes.
It describes others' or general situations objectively; avoid it for stating a personal reason about yourself.

examples.ja: 十年ぶりの優勝とあって、街全体がお祭り騒ぎになった。
examples.en: With it being their first championship in ten years, the whole town erupted into festivities.
examples.f: ｜十[じゅう]｜年[ねん]ぶりの｜優勝[ゆうしょう]とあって、｜街[まち]｜全体[ぜんたい]がお｜祭り騒[まつりさわ]ぎになった。

examples.ja: 連休最終日とあって、高速道路はどこも渋滞していた。
examples.en: Given that it was the last day of the long holiday, the expressways were jammed everywhere.
examples.f: ｜連休[れんきゅう]｜最終[さいしゅう]｜日[び]とあって、｜高速[こうそく]｜道路[どうろ]はどこも｜渋滞[じゅうたい]していた。

synonyms.note: だけあって praises a result as living up to what a quality would lead you to expect; とあって simply gives a special situation as the reason a natural result follows.
こととて offers a reason in a soft, apologetic, literary tone; とあって states a notable circumstance behind an unremarkable-to-expect result.

related.note: だけに stresses 'precisely because ~, all the more'; とあって leans on the situation being special or newsworthy.

entry.title: 〜とあれば
entry.meaning: if it is (a case of); if it's for the sake of ~
entry.summary: 〜とあれば sets up a special condition and says that, given it, one will readily do something one otherwise might not — 'if it's for ~, then...'. 子供のためとあれば = if it's for the children's sake, 必要とあれば = if it should prove necessary. The main clause usually expresses willing resolve or an inevitable response to that particular circumstance. It is more formal and weighty than a plain なら.
pitfalls: The condition is a special, weighty one that justifies the (often unusual) action that follows; it is stronger and more formal than a plain なら.
The main clause states a willing response or a natural consequence, not a neutral hypothetical.

examples.ja: お客様のご要望とあれば、できる限り対応いたします。
examples.en: If it is what the customer wishes, we will do our utmost to accommodate it.
examples.f: お｜客様[きゃくさま]のご｜要望[ようぼう]とあれば、できる｜限[かぎ]り｜対応[たいおう]いたします。

examples.ja: 恩師の頼みとあれば、断るわけにはいかない。
examples.en: If it's a request from my old teacher, I can hardly refuse.
examples.f: ｜恩師[おんし]の｜頼[たの]みとあれば、｜断[ことわ]るわけにはいかない。

synonyms.note: なら is a general 'if / in that case'; とあれば adds that the condition is special enough to prompt a willing or inevitable response.

related.note: とあって treats the special situation as an actual fact behind a result; とあれば treats it as a supposed condition prompting resolve.

entry.title: 〜といい〜といい
entry.meaning: both ~ and ~; whether you look at ~ or ~ (in every respect)
entry.summary: 〜といい〜といい picks out two representative aspects of something and comments that, judging by both, an overall evaluation holds — 'both ~ and ~'. 色といいデザインといい = in both color and design, 味といい香りといい = both in taste and aroma. The speaker cites two examples to back a subjective judgment about the whole, and the closing clause is that evaluation, often admiration or criticism.
pitfalls: It takes two nouns naming aspects or examples and leads to a subjective evaluation of the whole; the final clause is a judgment, not a neutral fact.
Different from 〜も〜も (plain 'both'): といい〜といい frames the two as evidence for an overall impression.

examples.ja: この旅館は、料理といい景色といい、申し分がなかった。
examples.en: This inn, in both its cuisine and its scenery, left nothing to be desired.
examples.f: この｜旅館[りょかん]は、｜料理[りょうり]といい｜景色[けしき]といい、｜申し分[もうしぶん]がなかった。

examples.ja: 態度といい言葉遣いといい、彼のふるまいには失望させられた。
examples.en: In both his attitude and his choice of words, his conduct was disappointing.
examples.f: ｜態度[たいど]といい｜言葉[ことば]｜遣[づか]いといい、｜彼[かれ]のふるまいには｜失望[しつぼう]させられた。

related.note: といわず〜といわず means 'not just these two but everywhere, without distinction'; といい〜といい lists two aspects to support an overall evaluation.

entry.title: 〜といえども
entry.meaning: even; even though; although one may say ~
entry.summary: 〜といえども concedes a point and then states something that holds despite it — 'even ~, even though it is ~'. プロといえども = even a professional, 子供といえども = even though they're just a child. It grants that the subject is X, yet the following clause runs against the expectation X would create. It is formal, somewhat literary, and often pairs with a sweeping generalization.
pitfalls: It concedes 'even (granting that it's) ~' and then states a contrary point; it is more formal and emphatic than ても or とはいえ.
The following clause goes against what the conceded point would lead you to expect.

examples.ja: どんなに小さなミスといえども、命に関わる場面では許されない。
examples.en: Even the smallest mistake is unforgivable in a situation where lives are at stake.
examples.f: どんなに｜小[ちい]さなミスといえども、｜命[いのち]に｜関[かか]わる｜場面[ばめん]では｜許[ゆる]されない。

examples.ja: いかに大企業といえども、時代の変化に対応できなければ生き残れない。
examples.en: Even a large corporation, however big, cannot survive if it fails to adapt to the changing times.
examples.f: いかに｜大[だい]｜企業[きぎょう]といえども、｜時代[じだい]の｜変化[へんか]に｜対応[たいおう]できなければ｜生き残[いきのこ]れない。

synonyms.note: ても is the everyday 'even if / even though'; といえども says the same with a formal, literary, concessive weight.

related.note: ものの concedes an established fact then notes it fell short of expectation; といえども concedes a category ('even a ~') before a contrary rule.
ながらも marks 'although, despite ~' between two facts of one subject; といえども concedes a generalized case.

entry.title: 〜といったらない・〜ったらない
entry.kana: といったらない・ったらない
entry.meaning: extremely; indescribably; ~ beyond words
entry.summary: 〜といったらない (casual 〜ったらない) marks a degree so extreme that words fail — 'you can't describe how ~ it is'. うれしいといったらない = indescribably happy, 悔しいったらない = frustrated beyond words. It attaches mainly to adjectives (and some nouns) naming a strong impression and pushes it to the utmost. It is emotive and colloquial, most often about negative feelings but usable for positive extremes too.
pitfalls: It pushes a quality to its extreme ('~ beyond description'), not a middling degree.
ったらない is the more casual, spoken contraction; といったらない is the fuller form.

examples.ja: 一日じゅう並んで、結局買えなかったのだから、情けないといったらない。
examples.en: After lining up all day and still not getting one, it was pathetic beyond words.
examples.f: ｜一[いち]｜日[にち]じゅう｜並[なら]んで、｜結局[けっきょく]｜買[か]えなかったのだから、｜情[なさ]けないといったらない。

examples.ja: 静まり返った夜の山道の心細さといったらなかった。
examples.en: The loneliness of that hushed mountain path at night was beyond describing.
examples.f: ｜静まり返[しずまりかえ]った｜夜[よる]の｜山道[さんどう]の｜心細[こころぼそ]さといったらなかった。

synonyms.note: この上ない states 'the utmost, none higher' rather formally; といったらない voices the same extremity with emotive, colloquial force.
限りだ intensifies an emotion adjective ('extremely ~'); といったらない adds the nuance that the degree defies description.

entry.title: 〜ときたら
entry.meaning: when it comes to ~ (with exasperation); as for ~
entry.summary: 〜ときたら singles out a topic — usually a person or thing close to the speaker — and leads into a complaint or exasperated remark about it. うちの息子ときたら = as for my son (honestly...), この天気ときたら = this weather, of all things. It sets up the topic with a fed-up, critical attitude, so the following comment is typically negative. It is colloquial and emotive.
pitfalls: The comment that follows is almost always a complaint or criticism; it carries an exasperated tone, not a neutral 'as for'.
The topic is usually someone or something familiar to the speaker; don't use it for distant, respectful reference.

examples.ja: うちの課長ときたら、自分のミスを絶対に認めようとしない。
examples.en: My section chief, honestly — he will never once admit his own mistakes.
examples.f: うちの｜課長[かちょう]ときたら、｜自分[じぶん]のミスを｜絶対[ぜったい]に｜認[みと]めようとしない。

examples.ja: 最近の若い者ときたら、挨拶の一つもまともにできないのか。
examples.en: The young folks these days — can't they even manage a proper greeting?
examples.f: ｜最近[さいきん]の｜若[わか]い｜者[もの]ときたら、｜挨拶[あいさつ]の｜一[ひと]つもまともにできないのか。

synonyms.note: とは reacts with surprise or evaluation to a fact ('to think that ~'); ときたら fixes a familiar topic and grumbles about it.

related.note: ときている piles on an extra clinching reason; ときたら opens a topic to complain about.

entry.title: 〜とは
entry.meaning: to think that ~!; the very idea that ~
entry.summary: In its emotive use, 〜とは reacts with surprise, shock, admiration, or dismay to a fact — 'to think that ~!'. まさか彼が犯人だったとは = to think he was the culprit. The sentence often trails off after とは, leaving the reaction (驚いた, 情けない...) unspoken. It is a little more formal or written than the colloquial なんて. Separately, とは also serves as a defining marker ('X とは Y' = X means Y).
pitfalls: In the emotive use the sentence often breaks off after とは (…とは！／…とは思わなかった), the reaction left unsaid.
Keep this surprise とは separate from the defining とは, which explains what a term means ('X means Y').

examples.ja: こんな所で君に会うとは、思ってもみなかった。
examples.en: To run into you in a place like this — I never even imagined it.
examples.f: こんな｜所[ところ]で｜君[きみ]に｜会[あ]うとは、｜思[おも]ってもみなかった。

examples.ja: あの真面目な彼が会社を辞めるとは、驚きだ。
examples.en: For that earnest fellow to quit the company — what a surprise.
examples.f: あの｜真面目[まじめ]な｜彼[かれ]が｜会社[かいしゃ]を｜辞[や]めるとは、｜驚[おどろ]きだ。

synonyms.note: なんて is the colloquial 'to think that ~!'; とは carries a slightly more formal, written tone.

related.note: ことか exclaims over a degree ('how very ~!'); とは reacts with surprise that a fact is even the case.

entry.title: 〜とばかりに
entry.meaning: as if to say ~; with a manner that all but says ~
entry.summary: 〜とばかりに attaches a quoted thought to someone's behavior: they don't actually speak the words, but their manner or action conveys them — 'as if to say ~'. 帰れとばかりに、彼はドアを指さした = he pointed at the door as if to say 'get out'. It often accompanies a vivid gesture or a decisive move, and captures the attitude the person is broadcasting without words.
pitfalls: The quoted words are not actually spoken — they render the attitude the person's manner conveys.
Do not confuse it with とばかり思っていた ('I was firmly convinced that ~'), which is unrelated.

examples.ja: 待ってましたとばかりに、子供たちは公園へ駆け出した。
examples.en: As if they'd been waiting for just this, the children dashed off to the park.
examples.f: ｜待[ま]ってましたとばかりに、｜子供[こども]たちは｜公園[こうえん]へ｜駆け出[かけだ]した。

examples.ja: 彼は早く帰れとばかりに、時計をちらちら見ていた。
examples.en: He kept glancing at the clock as if to say I should hurry home.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]は｜早[はや]く｜帰[かえ]れとばかりに、｜時計[とけい]をちらちら｜見[み]ていた。

entry.title: 〜ないまでも
entry.meaning: even if not (to that extent), at least ~
entry.summary: 〜ないまでも sets up a high standard that is not reached, then falls back on a lower but still meaningful one: 'even if not ~, at least ~'. 毎日とは言わないまでも = even if not every day (at least often). It attaches to a negated verb (often 〜とは言わない, 〜できない) and the second clause states the more modest expectation or wish that does hold.
pitfalls: The first clause names a level NOT attained; the second clause gives the lower bar that still applies, so keep the two in that order.
Do not confuse it with 〜までもない ('no need to go so far as to'): ないまでも concedes a lesser degree, までもない dismisses the action as unnecessary.

examples.ja: 満点とは言わないまでも、合格点は取りたい。
examples.en: Even if not a perfect score, I at least want to get a passing mark.
examples.f: ｜満点[まんてん]とは｜言[い]わないまでも、｜合格[ごうかく]｜点[てん]は｜取[と]りたい。

examples.ja: 完璧に理解できないまでも、要点だけは押さえておきたい。
examples.en: Even if I can't grasp it perfectly, I at least want to pin down the key points.
examples.f: ｜完璧[かんぺき]に｜理解[りかい]できないまでも、｜要点[ようてん]だけは｜押[お]さえておきたい。

related.note: までもない says the action is not even worth doing; ないまでも grants that a full degree isn't met but a partial one still stands.

entry.title: 〜ないものでもない
entry.meaning: it's not entirely impossible; it's not that ~ can't be done
entry.summary: 〜ないものでもない piles up negatives to make a grudging, hedged admission of possibility: 'it's not as though ~ couldn't be'. やってやれないものでもない = it's not that it can't be done (given the right conditions). It often follows a potential-negative verb and signals reluctant, conditional agreement — the speaker allows the possibility without fully committing to it.
structure: Verb［ない form］＋ものでもない
pitfalls: The tone is reluctant and qualified ('I suppose it could be'), not enthusiastic; it usually comes with a condition attached.
Count the negatives: ないものでもない resolves to a cautious positive, so 引き受けないものでもない means 'I might take it on', not 'I won't'.

examples.ja: 条件次第では、引き受けないものでもない。
examples.en: Depending on the terms, it's not as though I wouldn't take it on.
examples.f: ｜条件[じょうけん]｜次第[しだい]では、｜引き受[ひきう]けないものでもない。

examples.ja: 練習すれば、彼女に追いつけないものでもないだろう。
examples.en: With practice, it's not entirely impossible to catch up with her.
examples.f: ｜練習[れんしゅう]すれば、｜彼女[かのじょ]に｜追[お]いつけないものでもないだろう。

synonyms.note: ないでもない makes the same grudging concession more compactly; ないものでもない adds もの and sounds a touch more deliberative.

related.note: ないことはない also means 'it's not impossible'; ものでもない tends to feel more hedged and reluctant.

entry.title: 〜なくしては
entry.meaning: without ~ (it would be impossible)
entry.summary: 〜なくしては presents something as an indispensable condition: 'without ~, ... could not happen'. 努力なくしては成功はない = without effort there is no success. It attaches to a noun (or 〜することなくして) and the second clause is negative or denies a possibility, stressing that the named thing is the very thing everything hinges on. The tone is formal and often rhetorical.
pitfalls: The main clause must be negative or a denied possibility (〜ない, 〜えない); without which the pattern doesn't make sense.
It is formal and emphatic, common in speeches and writing — heavier than the everyday なしでは.

examples.ja: 皆様のご支援なくしては、この事業の成功はありえませんでした。
examples.en: Without all of your support, the success of this undertaking would have been impossible.
examples.f: ｜皆様[みなさま]のご｜支援[しえん]なくしては、この｜事業[じぎょう]の｜成功[せいこう]はありえませんでした。

examples.ja: 相互の信頼なくして、真の協力関係は築けない。
examples.en: Without mutual trust, no genuine partnership can be built.
examples.f: ｜相互[そうご]の｜信頼[しんらい]なくして、｜真[しん]の｜協力[きょうりょく]｜関係[かんけい]は｜築[きづ]けない。

synonyms.note: なしに／なしで plainly means 'without doing'; なくしては frames the thing as indispensable and pairs with a negative outcome.

related.note: ことなしに means 'without doing (an action)'; なくしては typically takes a noun and asserts that the result is impossible without it.

entry.title: 〜ならまだしも
entry.meaning: if it were ~ that would be one thing, but ~
entry.summary: 〜ならまだしも grants that one case would be comparatively acceptable, so as to condemn the actual, worse case: 一度だけならまだしも = if it were just once that would be tolerable, but... The case before it is 'still passable'; the main clause then registers that reality goes beyond that and is unacceptable or hard to accept.
pitfalls: What precedes it is presented as the lesser, still-bearable option; the complaint lands on the actual situation that follows.
Close to plain まだしも (N2), but ならまだしも specifically pins the 'acceptable' case to a condition ('if it were ~').

examples.ja: 一度だけならまだしも、同じ過ちを何度も繰り返すとは。
examples.en: If it were just once that would be one thing, but to repeat the same mistake over and over...
examples.f: ｜一[いち]｜度[ど]だけならまだしも、｜同[おな]じ｜過[あやま]ちを｜何[なん]｜度[ど]も｜繰り返[くりかえ]すとは。

examples.ja: 安いならまだしも、この品質でこの値段では買う気になれない。
examples.en: If it were cheap it would be another matter, but at this quality for this price I can't bring myself to buy it.
examples.f: ｜安[やす]いならまだしも、この｜品質[ひんしつ]でこの｜値段[ねだん]では｜買[か]う｜気[き]になれない。

synonyms.note: まだしも on its own means 'comparatively better / still acceptable'; ならまだしも fixes that acceptable case to an explicit condition.
ならいざ知らず brushes a case aside as 'who's to say'; ならまだしも rates it as 'tolerable by comparison', both to condemn the real case.

entry.title: 〜なり
entry.meaning: as soon as; the moment (one does) ~
entry.summary: Verb［dictionary form］＋なり means the second action follows the very instant the first is done: 家に帰るなり寝てしまった = the moment he got home, he fell asleep. The second event is typically sudden, spontaneous, and a bit unexpected, and both usually share one subject. It is literary. Note the separate た-form use 〜たなり ('left in that unchanged state'), as in 横になったなり.
structure: Verb［た form］＋なり ［left in that state］
pitfalls: Use the dictionary form for the 'as soon as' sense (見るなり), not the past tense.
The second clause describes an actual, often surprising event — not a command, intention, or request.
Distinguish 〜たなり ('remaining in that state', like 〜たまま), e.g. 靴を履いたなり寝る, from the 'the moment ~' sense.

examples.ja: 彼はドアを開けるなり、大声で叫び始めた。
examples.en: The moment he opened the door, he started shouting at the top of his voice.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]はドアを｜開[あ]けるなり、｜大声[おおごえ]で｜叫[さけ]び｜始[はじ]めた。

examples.ja: 子供は母親の顔を見るなり、わっと泣き出した。
examples.en: The instant the child saw its mother's face, it burst into tears.
examples.f: ｜子供[こども]は｜母親[ははおや]の｜顔[かお]を｜見[み]るなり、わっと｜泣[な]き｜出[だ]した。

synonyms.note: や否や is a similar literary 'as soon as'; なり leans harder on the second action being spontaneous and unexpected.
が早いか stresses that the two events were almost simultaneous; なり foregrounds the abrupt reaction that immediately follows.

related.note: か〜ないかのうちに says the second event began before the first fully finished; なり has the first clearly complete, then the reaction right after.

entry.title: なり〜なり
entry.meaning: either ~ or ~ (for instance); ~ or ~ or something
entry.summary: なり〜なり lists two representative options and invites the listener to pick one (or something in that vein): 電話なりメールなりで連絡して = get in touch by phone or email or whatever works. It attaches to nouns or dictionary-form verbs. The list is illustrative rather than exhaustive, and it commonly appears in suggestions or gentle instructions.
pitfalls: The two items are examples, not the only choices; 'or something along those lines' is implied.
Don't confuse the paired なり〜なり (choices) with the single なり ('as soon as').

examples.ja: わからないことがあれば、辞書で調べるなり先生に聞くなりしなさい。
examples.en: If there's something you don't understand, look it up in a dictionary or ask the teacher or something.
examples.f: わからないことがあれば、｜辞書[じしょ]で｜調[しら]べるなり｜先生[せんせい]に｜聞[き]くなりしなさい。

examples.ja: 電話なりメールなり、都合のいい方法で連絡してください。
examples.en: Get in touch by phone or email — whichever is convenient for you.
examples.f: ｜電話[でんわ]なりメールなり、｜都合[つごう]のいい｜方法[ほうほう]で｜連絡[れんらく]してください。

synonyms.note: たり〜たり lists representative actions that occur; なり〜なり lists options offered for the listener to choose among.
か〜か presents a plain 'either A or B' choice; なり〜なり adds an 'or something like that, whichever suits' flavor.

entry.title: 〜なりに・〜なりの
entry.meaning: in one's own way; in a manner fitting to ~
entry.summary: 〜なりに (adverbial) and 〜なりの (before a noun) mean 'in a way befitting the person or thing, within its own means': 私なりに考えた = I thought it over in my own way, 子供なりの理屈 = a child's own kind of logic. It respectfully acknowledges that someone did their best according to their own, often limited, capacity or position, without treating that as a shortcoming.
pitfalls: It implies doing one's best within one's own (often modest) means, and is not meant as a put-down.
Use なりに to modify a verb (私なりに頑張る) and なりの to modify a noun (私なりの答え).

examples.ja: 私なりに精一杯やったつもりだ。
examples.en: I did my very best in my own way, or so I believe.
examples.f: ｜私[わたし]なりに｜精一杯[せいいっぱい]やったつもりだ。

examples.ja: 子供には子供なりの理屈があるものだ。
examples.en: Children have their own kind of logic, in their own way.
examples.f: ｜子供[こども]には｜子供[こども]なりの｜理屈[りくつ]があるものだ。

related.note: らしい ('typical of / befitting', as in 子供らしい) judges by an expected image; なりの credits each one's own particular way of doing things.

entry.title: 〜には当たらない
entry.meaning: there's no need to; it's not worth (praising, being surprised, etc.)
entry.summary: 〜には当たらない says a certain reaction is not warranted — there's no need to be surprised, impressed, or to blame someone. 驚くには当たらない = no need to be surprised, 非難するには当たらない = not something to condemn. It attaches to a dictionary-form verb, most often a verb of emotional reaction, and calmly dismisses that the reaction is called for.
pitfalls: It pairs typically with reaction verbs (驚く・感心する・褒める・非難する) and says the reaction is unwarranted, not that something 'doesn't apply'.
Use the dictionary form: 驚くには当たらない, not 驚いたには当たらない.

examples.ja: 彼が優勝したからといって、驚くには当たらない。実力どおりだ。
examples.en: Just because he won is no reason to be surprised — it's exactly what his ability warranted.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]が｜優勝[ゆうしょう]したからといって、｜驚[おどろ]くには｜当[あ]たらない。｜実力[じつりょく]どおりだ。

examples.ja: あの程度のミスなら、そう責めるには当たらないよ。
examples.en: For a slip of that degree, there's really no need to blame him so harshly.
examples.f: あの｜程度[ていど]のミスなら、そう｜責[せ]めるには｜当[あ]たらないよ。

synonyms.note: には及ばない also means 'no need to', but is a shade more about sparing effort; には当たらない dismisses an emotional reaction as unwarranted.
ことはない is the everyday 'there's no need to ~'; には当たらない is formal and typically follows reaction verbs.

entry.title: 〜にあって
entry.meaning: in; at; under (a particular situation, position, or era)
entry.summary: 〜にあって places the following statement within a special situation, position, or time — 'being in ~, situated in ~'. 非常時にあって = in a time of emergency, その立場にあって = holding that position. It sets up circumstances that are notable or extreme, and the main clause tells what holds true under them. The negative-conditional form にあっても means 'even in ~'. It is a formal, written expression.
pitfalls: Formal and written; in ordinary speech に or で is used instead.
にあって frames a situation or position, not a physical meeting; do not read it as the 〜に会って ('meet ~') of everyday verbs.
にあっても means 'even in ~', shifting the sense from setting a scene to concession.

examples.ja: 危機的な状況にあって、彼は最後まで冷静さを失わなかった。
examples.en: In a critical situation, he kept his composure to the very end.
examples.f: ｜危機[きき]｜的[てき]な｜状況[じょうきょう]にあって、｜彼[かれ]は｜最後[さいご]まで｜冷静[れいせい]さを｜失[うしな]わなかった。

examples.ja: 情報が氾濫する現代にあっては、何を信じるかがかえって難しい。
examples.en: In today's world awash with information, deciding what to believe is, if anything, all the harder.
examples.f: ｜情報[じょうほう]が｜氾濫[はんらん]する｜現代[げんだい]にあっては、｜何[なに]を｜信[しん]じるかがかえって｜難[むずか]しい。

synonyms.note: において neutrally marks a place, time, or field; にあって stresses being placed within a notable or trying situation.

related.note: とあって gives a special circumstance as the reason for what follows; にあって sets the circumstance as a backdrop without asserting cause.

entry.title: 〜に難くない
entry.meaning: not hard to (imagine, guess, surmise)
entry.summary: 〜に難くない means that something takes no effort to imagine or infer — 'it is not hard to ~'. In practice it combines with only a few verbs, above all 想像する and 察する: 想像に難くない = not hard to imagine, 察するに難くない = not hard to surmise. It is used to say that a feeling or situation can readily be understood. The register is formal and literary.
pitfalls: It pairs almost exclusively with 想像する and 察する; it is not a general-purpose 'easy to do'.
With 想像 the fixed shape is 想像に難くない (the する drops); do not force it onto arbitrary verbs.
Formal and written — it would sound stiff in casual conversation.

examples.ja: 突然家族を失った彼の悲しみは、想像に難くない。
examples.en: The grief of a man who suddenly lost his family is not hard to imagine.
examples.f: ｜突然[とつぜん]｜家族[かぞく]を｜失[うしな]った｜彼[かれ]の｜悲[かな]しみは、｜想像[そうぞう]に｜難[かた]くない。

examples.ja: 彼女がこの数年どれほど苦労したかは、察するに難くない。
examples.en: It is not hard to surmise how much hardship she has been through these past few years.
examples.f: ｜彼女[かのじょ]がこの｜数[すう]｜年[ねん]どれほど｜苦労[くろう]したかは、｜察[さっ]するに｜難[かた]くない。

entry.title: 〜にして
entry.meaning: only at/when (a notable stage); and at the same time; being both ~ and ~
entry.summary: 〜にして is a formal, literary connector with two main senses. One marks a notable stage or degree — 五十歳にして = at (the age of) fifty, 今にして思えば = now that I look back. The other joins two qualities in one subject — 学者にして詩人 = a scholar and at the same time a poet. In both, にして links a noun to what is remarkable about that point or pairing. Context tells the senses apart.
pitfalls: Formal and literary; it would sound archaic or lofty in casual speech.
One sense marks a striking stage or degree ('only at ~'); the other means 'being both A and B' — context disambiguates.
Do not confuse it with にしては ('for ~, considering ~') or にしても ('even ~'); those are different compounds.

examples.ja: 彼は五十歳にして、ようやく自分の天職を見つけた。
examples.en: At fifty, he at last found his true calling.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]は｜五[ご]｜十[じゅう]｜歳[さい]にして、ようやく｜自分[じぶん]の｜天職[てんしょく]を｜見[み]つけた。

examples.ja: 彼女は優れた研究者にして、二児の母でもある。
examples.en: She is an accomplished researcher and, at the same time, a mother of two.
examples.f: ｜彼女[かのじょ]は｜優[すぐ]れた｜研究[けんきゅう]｜者[しゃ]にして、｜二[に]｜児[じ]の｜母[はは]でもある。

related.note: にしては means 'for ~, considering ~' and judges against a standard; the bare にして marks a notable stage or a pairing of qualities.
こそ singles out and emphasizes a word; にして in its 'only at ~' sense likewise highlights a stage as pivotal, but formally and with a noun.

entry.title: 〜に即して
entry.meaning: in accordance with; in line with (facts, reality, rules)
entry.summary: 〜に即して means acting in keeping with a concrete standard such as the facts, reality, law, or one's experience — 'in line with ~, grounded in ~'. 現実に即した対策 = measures grounded in reality, 規則に即して判断する = judge in accordance with the rules. It stresses fitting one's response to how things actually are, not to abstract ideals. The adnominal form is に即した, and the register is formal.
pitfalls: It pairs with concrete standards — 実情・現実・事実・法律・経験 — not with personal wishes or feelings.
Distinguish it from に沿って ('along / following a line, plan, or intention'); 即して means conforming to the actual facts.

examples.ja: 理想論ではなく、現実に即した対策が求められている。
examples.en: What's needed are measures grounded in reality, not idealistic arguments.
examples.f: ｜理想[りそう]｜論[ろん]ではなく、｜現実[げんじつ]に｜即[そく]した｜対策[たいさく]が｜求[もと]められている。

examples.ja: 規則に即して、公平に処分を決めるべきだ。
examples.en: The penalty should be decided fairly, in accordance with the rules.
examples.f: ｜規則[きそく]に｜即[そく]して、｜公平[こうへい]に｜処分[しょぶん]を｜決[き]めるべきだ。

synonyms.note: に照らして checks something against a standard or precedent to judge it; に即して means shaping one's response to fit the actual facts.

related.note: に基づいて uses something as a foundation or grounds to build on; に即して means staying faithful to the concrete facts or rules.
に沿って means following along a line, plan, or wish; に即して means conforming to how things actually are.

entry.title: 〜に耐える・〜に耐えない
entry.kana: にたえる・にたえない
entry.meaning: worth doing / holds up to ~ ; unbearable to ~ ; filled with (emotion)
entry.summary: 〜に耐える means something is solid enough to be worth doing or can withstand scrutiny — 鑑賞に耐える = worth appreciating, 批判に耐える = holds up to criticism. Its negative 〜に耐えない has two uses: with 見る・聞く it means 'too awful to ~' (見るに耐えない = unbearable to watch), and with emotion nouns like 感謝・感慨 it means 'filled with ~' (感謝の念に耐えない). It is formal, and に堪えない is the same word spelled differently.
structure: Verb［dictionary form］＋に耐える／に耐えない
pitfalls: 〜に耐える = 'worth ~ing / holds up to ~'; 〜に耐えない = 'unbearable to ~' (with 見る・聞く) or 'filled with ~' (with 感謝・感慨).
に堪えない is merely a different spelling of the same expression, not a separate pattern.

examples.ja: この作品は、大人の鑑賞にも耐える完成度だ。
examples.en: This work is polished enough to be worth appreciating even by adults.
examples.f: この｜作品[さくひん]は、｜大人[おとな]の｜鑑賞[かんしょう]にも｜耐[た]える｜完成[かんせい]｜度[ど]だ。

examples.ja: 彼らの口論は、とても聞くに耐えないものだった。
examples.en: Their quarrel was truly unbearable to listen to.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]らの｜口論[こうろん]は、とても｜聞[き]くに｜耐[た]えないものだった。

synonyms.note: に値する means 'is worth / deserves ~' as a positive judgment; に耐える means it is solid enough to hold up to something like appreciation.

related.note: に足りない means 'not worth ~ing / not enough to'; に耐えない means 'unbearable to ~' or 'filled with (emotion)'.
に忍びない is 'too pitiful to bear'; 見るに耐えない is 'too unpleasant to keep watching' — sympathy versus distaste.

entry.title: 〜に足る・〜に足りる
entry.meaning: worthy of; sufficient to; enough to warrant
entry.summary: 〜に足る marks that something is worth doing or sufficient to justify a response — 信頼するに足る人物 = a person worthy of trust, 満足するに足る成果 = results good enough to be satisfied with. It attaches to a verb in dictionary form (or a noun) and is formal, written Japanese. The negative 〜に足りない ('not worth ~') is very common, especially in the fixed phrase 取るに足りない ('trivial, not worth mentioning').
pitfalls: The negative 〜に足りない means 'not worth ~'; 取るに足りない is a set phrase meaning 'trivial, insignificant'.
Attach it to the dictionary form: 信頼するに足る, not 信頼したに足る.

examples.ja: 彼はこの大役を任せるに足る人物だと思う。
examples.en: I think he is a person worthy of being entrusted with this major role.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]はこの｜大役[たいやく]を｜任[まか]せるに｜足[た]る｜人物[じんぶつ]だと｜思[おも]う。

examples.ja: その程度の失敗は、いちいち気にするに足りない。
examples.en: A failure of that degree isn't worth fretting over one by one.
examples.f: その｜程度[ていど]の｜失敗[しっぱい]は、いちいち｜気[き]にするに｜足[た]りない。

synonyms.note: に値する also means 'worth ~'; に足る is more literary and leans on 'sufficient to warrant'.
に恥じない frames worth as 'living up to (a name/standard)'; に足る frames it as 'good enough to justify (an action)'.

entry.title: 〜にとどまらず
entry.meaning: not stopping at; not limited to; not only
entry.summary: 〜にとどまらず says that something does not stop at the first item but extends further, to something larger or wider — 国内にとどまらず海外にも = not limited to the domestic market but reaching abroad too. It attaches to a noun or a plain-form clause, and the second clause typically widens the scope with も, まで, or a comparable marker. This is formal, written Japanese.
pitfalls: The point is that the scope reaches beyond the first item to something broader; the follow-up clause usually carries も／まで.
It stresses spatial or conceptual expansion, unlike a plain 'not only ~ but also' list.

examples.ja: 被害は一つの村にとどまらず、周辺の地域全体に広がった。
examples.en: The damage did not stop at one village but spread across the entire surrounding region.
examples.f: ｜被害[ひがい]は｜一[ひと]つの｜村[むら]にとどまらず、｜周辺[しゅうへん]の｜地域[ちいき]｜全体[ぜんたい]に｜広[ひろ]がった。

examples.ja: 彼の関心は音楽にとどまらず、絵画や文学にまで及んでいる。
examples.en: His interests do not stop at music but extend even to painting and literature.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]の｜関心[かんしん]は｜音楽[おんがく]にとどまらず、｜絵画[かいが]や｜文学[ぶんがく]にまで｜及[およ]んでいる。

synonyms.note: のみならず is a general 'not only ~ but also'; にとどまらず specifically pictures the scope spilling beyond a boundary.
だけでなく is the everyday 'not only ~'; にとどまらず is formal and emphasizes reaching further out.

entry.title: 〜に引き換え
entry.meaning: in stark contrast to; unlike
entry.summary: 〜に引き換え sets two things side by side and draws a sharp, often evaluative contrast — one side clearly better or worse than the other. 兄に引き換え弟は… = unlike the older brother, the younger one… It attaches to a noun (or なの＋に引き換え after a clause). Unlike the neutral に対して, 〜に引き換え carries the speaker's judgment that the two differ markedly.
pitfalls: It carries a subjective, evaluative tone (one side is better or worse); に対して by contrast is a neutral juxtaposition.
Both compared items should be comparable in kind — two people, two years, two situations.

examples.ja: 去年の記録的な猛暑にひきかえ、今年の夏は驚くほど過ごしやすい。
examples.en: In stark contrast to last year's record heat, this summer is surprisingly pleasant.
examples.f: ｜去年[きょねん]の｜記録[きろく]｜的[てき]な｜猛暑[もうしょ]にひきかえ、｜今年[ことし]の｜夏[なつ]は｜驚[おどろ]くほど｜過[す]ごしやすい。

examples.ja: よく働く姉にひきかえ、弟はいつも遊んでばかりいる。
examples.en: Unlike his hard-working older sister, the younger brother is always just goofing off.
examples.f: よく｜働[はたら]く｜姉[あね]にひきかえ、｜弟[おとうと]はいつも｜遊[あそ]んでばかりいる。

synonyms.note: に反して means 'contrary to (an expectation)'; に引き換え contrasts two comparable things with an evaluative slant.
に対して is a neutral 'whereas / in contrast'; に引き換え adds the speaker's judgment that one side compares poorly.

entry.title: 〜の至り
entry.meaning: the height of; extreme (emotion); the utmost of
entry.summary: 〜の至り expresses that an emotion is felt at its utmost — 光栄の至り = the greatest of honors, 感激の至り = deeply moved beyond words. It attaches to a small set of emotion nouns and belongs to very formal, ceremonial or humble speech. The fixed phrase 若気の至り ('the folly of youth') is a notable exception, naming a rash act driven by youthful impulse.
pitfalls: It attaches to a limited set of emotion nouns (光栄・感激・恐縮・赤面); it is not a freely productive pattern.
若気の至り is a set idiom meaning 'a blunder of youthful impulsiveness', not an emotion at its peak.

examples.ja: このような名誉ある賞をいただき、光栄の至りでございます。
examples.en: To receive such an honorable award is the greatest of honors for me.
examples.f: このような｜名誉[めいよ]ある｜賞[しょう]をいただき、｜光栄[こうえい]の｜至[いた]りでございます。

examples.ja: 若気の至りとはいえ、当時の言動は今思うと恥ずかしい。
examples.en: Though it was the folly of youth, my words and deeds back then are embarrassing to recall now.
examples.f: ｜若気[わかげ]の｜至[いた]りとはいえ、｜当時[とうじ]の｜言動[げんどう]は｜今[いま]｜思[おも]うと｜恥[は]ずかしい。

synonyms.note: の極み marks a state pushed to its limit (贅沢・混乱); の至り is reserved for emotions at their peak in humble set phrases.
限りだ also expresses an emotion at its extreme (うれしい限りだ); の至り is more formal and attaches to emotion nouns.

entry.title: のみならず
entry.meaning: not only ~ but also
entry.summary: のみならず means 'not only ~ but also,' the formal counterpart of だけでなく. It states one fact and then adds a further, often broader one: 国内のみならず海外でも = not only domestically but abroad as well. It attaches to nouns and plain-form clauses, and the second part is frequently marked with も. The register is formal and written.
pitfalls: It is formal and written; conversationally だけでなく is the natural choice.
The added element is usually equal to or larger in scope than the first, often marked with も.

examples.ja: この小説は国内のみならず、海外でも高く評価されている。
examples.en: This novel is highly regarded not only within Japan but abroad as well.
examples.f: この｜小説[しょうせつ]は｜国内[こくない]のみならず、｜海外[かいがい]でも｜高[たか]く｜評価[ひょうか]されている。

examples.ja: 彼は知識が豊富であるのみならず、それを分かりやすく伝える力もある。
examples.en: He is not only rich in knowledge but also has the ability to convey it clearly.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]は｜知識[ちしき]が｜豊富[ほうふ]であるのみならず、それを｜分[わ]かりやすく｜伝[つた]える｜力[ちから]もある。

synonyms.note: だけでなく is the everyday 'not only ~ but also'; のみならず is its formal equivalent.
ばかりか 'not only ~ but even' highlights an escalating, often surprising addition; のみならず is more neutral and formal.
にとどまらず 'not stopping at ~' stresses going beyond a limit; のみならず simply adds a further element.

related.note: はもちろん 'not to mention' treats the first item as obvious; のみならず adds a further point in formal prose.

entry.title: 〜はおろか
entry.meaning: let alone; not to mention; to say nothing of
entry.summary: 〜はおろか says that not only the greater or more obvious thing but even a more basic one is (typically) not the case. 漢字はおろか、ひらがなも書けない = can't write even hiragana, let alone kanji. It attaches to a noun, and the second, more basic item is usually marked with も, さえ, or すら, in a generally negative sentence. This is formal, written Japanese.
pitfalls: The second item (marked も／さえ／すら) is the more basic case, and the whole sentence is usually negative.
It attaches to nouns; the emphasis is 'even the obvious thing doesn't hold, never mind the harder one'.

examples.ja: 大けがをして、走ることはおろか、歩くことさえままならない。
examples.en: After the serious injury, he can't even walk, let alone run.
examples.f: ｜大[だい]けがをして、｜走[はし]ることはおろか、｜歩[ある]くことさえままならない。

examples.ja: その村には電気はおろか、水道すら引かれていない。
examples.en: That village has no running water, let alone electricity.
examples.f: その｜村[むら]には｜電気[でんき]はおろか、｜水道[すいどう]すら｜引[ひ]かれていない。

synonyms.note: どころか can also reverse an expectation ('far from ~'); はおろか strictly builds a 'not even the basic thing' scale.
のみならず adds 'not only ~ but also' in positive statements; はおろか works in negatives ('let alone').

related.note: さえ ('even') often marks the second, basic item in a はおろか sentence.

entry.title: 〜ばこそ
entry.meaning: precisely because ~; it is only because ~
entry.summary: 〜ばこそ gives the true, emphatic reason behind a result — 'it is precisely because ~ that…'. 君を思えばこそ = it is precisely because I care about you. It attaches to the ば-conditional form (であればこそ after a noun or な-adjective), and the reason is usually a positive or heartfelt one. This is formal, somewhat literary Japanese, more elevated than からこそ.
pitfalls: It highlights the genuine underlying reason for a (usually positive) outcome; it is more formal and emphatic than からこそ.
The reason clause is often followed by のだ／んです, underscoring the explanation.

examples.ja: 君の将来を思えばこそ、あえて厳しいことを言うのだ。
examples.en: It is precisely because I care about your future that I dare to say these harsh things.
examples.f: ｜君[きみ]の｜将来[しょうらい]を｜思[おも]えばこそ、あえて｜厳[きび]しいことを｜言[い]うのだ。

examples.ja: 家族の支えがあればこそ、私は困難を乗り越えられた。
examples.en: It was only because I had my family's support that I could overcome the hardships.
examples.f: ｜家族[かぞく]の｜支[ささ]えがあればこそ、｜私[わたし]は｜困難[こんなん]を｜乗り越[のりこ]えられた。

synonyms.note: からこそ is the everyday emphatic 'precisely because'; ばこそ is more formal and literary.
こそ alone emphasizes a noun ('this very ~'); ばこそ emphasizes a reason clause ('precisely because ~').

entry.title: 〜ばそれまでだ・〜たらそれまでだ
entry.kana: ばそれまでだ・たらそれまでだ
entry.romaji: ba sore made da; tara sore made da
entry.meaning: if ~, then it's all over; if ~, that's the end of it
entry.summary: 〜ばそれまでだ / 〜たらそれまでだ says that if a certain (usually bad) thing happens, that is the end of everything — there is nothing more to be done and any effort so far comes to nothing. 見つかればそれまでだ = if we're found out, it's all over. It stresses that a single event would render everything else pointless.
pitfalls: The condition is typically an undesirable event that would nullify everything; the point is finality, not just 'up until then'.
It is often paired with a preceding 'no matter how much ~' clause to underline that all the effort would be wasted.

examples.ja: どんなに貯金しても、病気で倒れればそれまでだ。
examples.en: No matter how much you save, if you fall ill it's all over.
examples.f: どんなに｜貯金[ちょきん]しても、｜病気[びょうき]で｜倒[たお]れればそれまでだ。

examples.ja: 大事な書類だから、なくしたらそれまでだよ。
examples.en: It's an important document, so if you lose it, that's the end of it.
examples.f: ｜大事[だいじ]な｜書類[しょるい]だから、なくしたらそれまでだよ。

related.note: までだ plays an action down as 'merely ~'; ばそれまでだ declares that a condition would bring everything to a dead end.

entry.title: 〜べくもない
entry.meaning: cannot possibly ~; there is no way to ~
entry.summary: 〜べくもない is a literary way to say something is utterly impossible — 'cannot possibly ~, there is no way to ~'. 知るべくもない = there's no way one could know, 望むべくもない = cannot even be hoped for. It follows a dictionary-form verb and denies even the possibility, more emphatically and elegantly than ことができない.
pitfalls: Formal and literary; it conveys flat impossibility, stronger and more elegant than 〜ことができない.
It tends to attach to verbs of knowing, hoping, or comparing (知る, 望む, 比べる).

examples.ja: 当時の私に、その言葉の本当の意味など知るべくもなかった。
examples.en: There was no way that I, back then, could have known the true meaning of those words.
examples.f: ｜当時[とうじ]の｜私[わたし]に、その｜言葉[ことば]の｜本当[ほんとう]の｜意味[いみ]など｜知[し]るべくもなかった。

examples.ja: 一介の新人に、社長の真意を推し量るべくもない。
examples.en: A mere newcomer has no way of gauging the president's real intentions.
examples.f: ｜一介[いっかい]の｜新人[しんじん]に、｜社長[しゃちょう]の｜真意[しんい]を｜推し量[おしはか]るべくもない。

synonyms.note: ようがない ('there's no way to') is colloquial; べくもない is its literary counterpart.
かねる means one cannot bring oneself to / is unable to do; べくもない denies the very possibility outright.

related.note: べく shares the same root but expresses purpose ('in order to'), not impossibility.

entry.title: 〜まじき
entry.meaning: unbecoming of; that must not be (literary)
entry.summary: 〜まじき is a literary attributive meaning 'that must not be, unbecoming of' — it modifies a noun to condemn conduct as improper for a given role. 教師にあるまじき言動 = behaviour unbecoming of a teacher, 許すまじき罪 = an unforgivable crime. It descends from classical まじ (the negative of べし) and appears mostly in the set frame 〜にあるまじき.
pitfalls: Literary and largely frozen in 〜にあるまじき (＋ 行為／言動 etc.); it is not freely productive.
It labels conduct as improper for a role or status, so a person or position is usually named with に.

examples.ja: 情報を漏らすとは、公務員にあるまじき行為だ。
examples.en: Leaking information is conduct utterly unbecoming of a public servant.
examples.f: ｜情報[じょうほう]を｜漏[も]らすとは、｜公務員[こうむいん]にあるまじき｜行為[こうい]だ。

examples.ja: それは指導者としてあるまじき、無責任な発言だった。
examples.en: That was an irresponsible remark unworthy of a leader.
examples.f: それは｜指導[しどう]｜者[しゃ]としてあるまじき、｜無責任[むせきにん]な｜発言[はつげん]だった。

synonyms.note: べからず ends a clause as a prohibition; まじき modifies a noun attributively ('unbecoming ~').

related.note: べきだ ('should') is the affirmative; まじき functions as its literary negative counterpart.

entry.title: 〜までもない・〜までもなく
entry.kana: までもない・までもなく
entry.romaji: made mo nai; made mo naku
entry.meaning: there is no need to go so far as to ~; it goes without saying
entry.summary: 〜までもない says an action isn't worth taking because the matter is too obvious or minor to require it — 'there's no need to go so far as to ~'. 言うまでもない = it goes without saying, わざわざ確認するまでもない = no need to bother checking. The 〜までもなく form links to a following clause: 説明するまでもなく = without even needing to explain.
pitfalls: It marks an action as unnecessary because the point is self-evident or trivial, not that the action is forbidden.
The very common 言うまでもない / 言うまでもなく means 'needless to say'.

examples.ja: こんな簡単な計算は、電卓を使うまでもない。
examples.en: A calculation this simple doesn't call for a calculator.
examples.f: こんな｜簡単[かんたん]な｜計算[けいさん]は、｜電卓[でんたく]を｜使[つか]うまでもない。

examples.ja: 言うまでもなく、締め切りを守ることが何より大切だ。
examples.en: It goes without saying that meeting the deadline matters above all.
examples.f: ｜言[い]うまでもなく、｜締め切[しめき]りを｜守[まも]ることが｜何[なに]より｜大切[たいせつ]だ。

synonyms.note: ことはない says 'there's no need to ~'; までもない adds that it isn't worth going so far because the point is obvious.
ほどのことではない downplays how serious a matter is; までもない says an action is superfluous given how self-evident the point is.

related.note: までだ ('merely ~') is a different までだ construction expressing resolve or justification.

entry.title: 〜まみれ
entry.meaning: covered in; smeared all over with
entry.summary: 〜まみれ marks a surface covered or smeared all over with something — almost always a dirty, wet, or unpleasant substance. 泥まみれ = covered in mud, 汗まみれ = drenched in sweat, 血まみれ = covered in blood. It attaches to a noun and can extend to abstract unpleasantness clinging to someone: 借金まみれ = mired in debt.
pitfalls: The covering substance is typically unpleasant — mud, sweat, blood, dust, debt — not something clean or desirable.
It stresses being smeared all over a surface, unlike だらけ, which stresses 'full of lots of ~' (mistakes, people).

examples.ja: 子供たちは泥まみれになって、夕方まで川で遊んでいた。
examples.en: The children got covered in mud and played in the river until evening.
examples.f: ｜子供[こども]たちは｜泥[どろ]まみれになって、｜夕方[ゆうがた]まで｜川[かわ]で｜遊[あそ]んでいた。

examples.ja: 事業に失敗し、彼は借金まみれの生活を送っていた。
examples.en: Having failed in business, he was living a life mired in debt.
examples.f: ｜事業[じぎょう]に｜失敗[しっぱい]し、｜彼[かれ]は｜借金[しゃっきん]まみれの｜生活[せいかつ]を｜送[おく]っていた。

synonyms.note: だらけ stresses 'full of many ~'; まみれ stresses a substance smeared all over a surface.
ずくめ means 'nothing but ~' and can be positive (黒ずくめ, いいことずくめ); まみれ is always a dirty substance clinging to a surface.

entry.title: 〜めく・〜めいた
entry.meaning: to show signs of; to take on the air of; -like
entry.summary: The suffix めく attaches to a limited set of nouns to form a verb meaning 'to take on the atmosphere or signs of ~': 春めく = to grow spring-like, 謎めく = to become mysterious, 皮肉めく = to sound sarcastic. The adnominal past form めいた modifies a following noun — 謎めいた話 = a mysterious story, 冗談めいた口調 = a joking tone. It is a somewhat literary way to say something gives off a certain air without fully being that thing.
pitfalls: めく attaches only to a fixed set of nouns (春・謎・皮肉・冗談 etc.); it is not freely productive with any noun.
In front of a noun the past form めいた is used (謎めいた話), not めくた or めく話.

examples.ja: 三月に入り、日差しもようやく春めいてきた。
examples.en: Now that March has arrived, the sunlight has finally taken on a spring-like feel.
examples.f: ｜三月[さんがつ]に｜入[はい]り、｜日差[ひざ]しもようやく｜春[はる]めいてきた。

examples.ja: 彼の謎めいた笑みの意味を、誰も読み取れなかった。
examples.en: No one could read the meaning of his enigmatic smile.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]の｜謎[なぞ]めいた｜笑[え]みの｜意味[いみ]を、｜誰[だれ]も｜読み取[よみと]れなかった。

synonyms.note: らしい says something is typical of or behaves as befits its category; めく says it takes on the outward air of something it is not fully.
っぽい ('-ish') is colloquial and broadly productive; めく is literary and limited to set combinations.

entry.title: 〜もさることながら
entry.meaning: not only ~ but also (and even more so); ~ goes without saying, but
entry.summary: Noun ＋ もさることながら concedes that the first item is indeed remarkable ('~ is of course a given / goes without saying'), then directs attention to a second item as being just as noteworthy or even more so. この店は味もさることながら接客もすばらしい = the food here is excellent, of course, but the service is wonderful too. It is a formal, written-flavored expression used to praise or highlight two points while foregrounding the second.
pitfalls: The weight falls on what comes after; the first item is presented as already understood, and the second is stressed as equally or more important.
It attaches to nouns; it is formal and belongs to careful speech or writing, not casual conversation.

examples.ja: この旅館は料理もさることながら、窓から望む景色が実に見事だ。
examples.en: At this inn the cuisine is superb, of course, but the view from the window is truly magnificent.
examples.f: この｜旅館[りょかん]は｜料理[りょうり]もさることながら、｜窓[まど]から｜望[のぞ]む｜景色[けしき]が｜実[じつ]に｜見事[みごと]だ。

examples.ja: 語学の習得には、才能もさることながら、日々の地道な努力が欠かせない。
examples.en: In mastering a language, talent matters of course, but steady daily effort is indispensable.
examples.f: ｜語学[ごがく]の｜習得[しゅうとく]には、｜才能[さいのう]もさることながら、｜日々[ひび]の｜地道[じみち]な｜努力[どりょく]が｜欠[か]かせない。

synonyms.note: のみならず simply adds 'not only A but also B'; もさることながら additionally treats A as an acknowledged given and spotlights B.
ばかりか adds a further, often surprising item; もさることながら balances two notable points rather than escalating.

entry.title: 〜ものを
entry.meaning: if only ~; and yet (regret or reproach)
entry.summary: 〜ものを expresses regret or reproach that reality turned out differently from what could or should have been. It typically follows a hypothetical (〜ば／〜たら) describing the better outcome that failed to happen: 一言言ってくれればよかったものを = if only you'd said something. The tone is emotional and often faintly accusatory, and the sentence may trail off after ものを, leaving the complaint implied. It is literary and expressive.
pitfalls: It carries regret or reproach about a missed possibility; it is not the neutral のに and not the general ものだ.
The clause before ものを describes what would have been better, and reality fell short of it.

examples.ja: 一言相談してくれれば手を貸せたものを、彼は誰にも言わずに抱え込んでしまった。
examples.en: If only he'd said a word to me, I could have helped, but he kept it all to himself and told no one.
examples.f: ｜一言[ひとこと]｜相談[そうだん]してくれれば｜手[て]を｜貸[か]せたものを、｜彼[かれ]は｜誰[だれ]にも｜言[い]わずに｜抱え込[かかえこ]んでしまった。

examples.ja: 素直に謝れば済んだものを、言い訳ばかりして事を大きくしてしまった。
examples.en: It would have been over if he'd simply apologized, and yet he only made excuses and blew things out of proportion.
examples.f: ｜素直[すなお]に｜謝[あやま]れば｜済[す]んだものを、｜言い訳[いいわけ]ばかりして｜事[こと]を｜大[おお]きくしてしまった。

related.note: くせに reproaches a person for acting against what their situation warrants; ものを laments a better outcome that a hypothetical could have secured.

entry.title: 〜や否や
entry.meaning: as soon as; the moment that; no sooner ~ than
entry.summary: 〜や否や attaches to a dictionary-form verb to mean 'the instant that ~, no sooner ~ than': ベルが鳴るや否や = the moment the bell rang. The second clause reports what happened immediately and unexpectedly right after. It is a literary, written expression; the following clause states an actual past event, not a plan, request, or command.
pitfalls: It is literary; in ordinary speech 〜とすぐに or 〜たとたん is more natural.
The second clause must be a factual, usually past, occurrence — not a command, request, or the speaker's own intention.

examples.ja: ベルが鳴るや否や、生徒たちは教室を飛び出していった。
examples.en: The moment the bell rang, the students dashed out of the classroom.
examples.f: ベルが｜鳴[な]るや｜否[いな]や、｜生徒[せいと]たちは｜教室[きょうしつ]を｜飛び出[とびだ]していった。

examples.ja: その知らせを聞くや否や、彼女は席を立って部屋を出て行った。
examples.en: No sooner had she heard the news than she rose from her seat and left the room.
examples.f: その｜知[し]らせを｜聞[き]くや｜否[いな]や、｜彼女[かのじょ]は｜席[せき]を｜立[た]って｜部屋[へや]を｜出[で]て｜行[い]った。

synonyms.note: が早いか is likewise literary 'the moment ~', but stresses that the second action began almost before the first was even finished.
たとたん(に) also means 'the moment ~', often with surprise, but is less literary and follows the た-form.
〜なり means 'as soon as ~' where the same subject moves straight into the next action; や否や allows a different subject or an external event to follow.

related.note: と同時に means 'at the same time as ~' (simultaneity); や否や stresses immediate succession right after the first event.

entry.title: ゆえに
entry.meaning: therefore; hence; because of; for the reason that (formal)
entry.summary: ゆえに expresses cause and consequence in formal, literary, or logical language. As a conjunction at the head of a sentence it means 'therefore, hence'. Attached to a noun (＋ゆえ／のゆえに) or a plain clause (＋がゆえに) it means 'owing to ~, because of ~': 経験の浅さゆえに = owing to inexperience. It is the register of reasoned argument and classical style, far more formal than から or ので.
pitfalls: This is formal/literary; in everyday speech から, ので, or だから are the natural choices.
When it attaches to a noun, no の is strictly required (若さゆえ), though のゆえに also occurs.

examples.ja: 彼の判断は、経験の浅さゆえに甘いところがあった。
examples.en: His judgment, owing to his lack of experience, was naive in places.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]の｜判断[はんだん]は、｜経験[けいけん]の｜浅[あさ]さゆえに｜甘[あま]いところがあった。

examples.ja: 前例のない事業である。ゆえに、慎重な検討が求められる。
examples.en: This is an unprecedented undertaking. Therefore, careful examination is called for.
examples.f: ｜前例[ぜんれい]のない｜事業[じぎょう]である。ゆえに、｜慎重[しんちょう]な｜検討[けんとう]が｜求[もと]められる。

synonyms.note: から is the everyday 'because'; ゆえに expresses the same causal link in formal, literary, or logical writing.
ため(に) gives a neutral cause or purpose; ゆえに is more formal and belongs to reasoned or classical style.

related.note: ので softens a reason as objective and polite; ゆえに is markedly formal and literary.

entry.title: 〜を皮切りに
entry.meaning: starting with; as the first of an unfolding series
entry.summary: 〜を皮切りに marks X as the first instance from which a series spreads or expands — 東京公演を皮切りに全国ツアーが始まった = starting with the Tokyo show, a nationwide tour began. 皮切り literally means 'the first cut', and the following clause must describe a chain of events or a spreading development that grows out of that opening, not a single isolated act. It is formal and often used of tours, movements, and cascading reactions.
structure: Noun［first event］＋を皮切りに（して）／を皮切りとして
pitfalls: What follows must be a series or spreading development that grows from the first instance — not a single, unconnected event.
The named event is genuinely the chronological start of the chain, giving it a sense of momentum picking up.

examples.ja: 東京公演を皮切りに、全国各地でのツアーが始まった。
examples.en: Starting with the Tokyo performance, a tour across the country got under way.
examples.f: ｜東京[とうきょう]｜公演[こうえん]を｜皮切[かわき]りに、｜全国[ぜんこく]｜各地[かくち]でのツアーが｜始[はじ]まった。

examples.ja: 彼の勇気ある発言を皮切りに、次々と改革を求める声が上がり始めた。
examples.en: Beginning with his courageous remark, calls for reform began to rise one after another.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]の｜勇気[ゆうき]ある｜発言[はつげん]を｜皮切[かわき]りに、｜次々[つぎつぎ]と｜改革[かいかく]を｜求[もと]める｜声[こえ]が｜上[あ]がり｜始[はじ]めた。

synonyms.note: をはじめ lists X as a representative example among others; を皮切りに marks X as the chronological first of a series that unfolds from it.

entry.title: 〜を機に
entry.meaning: taking ~ as the occasion/opportunity (for a change)
entry.summary: 〜を機に treats an event as the occasion that prompts a deliberate new action or change: 結婚を機に転職した = took marriage as the occasion to change jobs; 定年を機に = on the occasion of retirement. It is fairly formal, and the following clause is a chosen action, not an automatic consequence. 機 here is 'opportunity/turning point'.
pitfalls: The following clause is a deliberate action or change taken because of the event, not a spontaneous result.
Fairly formal; for everyday speech, をきっかけに feels more casual.

examples.ja: 定年を機に、夫婦で田舎に移り住むことにした。
examples.en: Taking his retirement as the occasion, the couple decided to move to the countryside.
examples.f: ｜定年[ていねん]を｜機[き]に、｜夫婦[ふうふ]で｜田舎[いなか]に｜移り住[うつりす]むことにした。

examples.ja: 今回の失敗を機に、業務の進め方を一から見直すことにした。
examples.en: Using this failure as a turning point, we decided to review our workflow from scratch.
examples.f: ｜今回[こんかい]の｜失敗[しっぱい]を｜機[き]に、｜業務[ぎょうむ]の｜進め方[すすめかた]を｜一[いち]から｜見直[みなお]すことにした。

synonyms.note: を契機に is near-identical in meaning and slightly more formal/literary; を機に is the shorter everyday equivalent.
をきっかけに is the more colloquial 'triggered by'; を機に is more formal and leans toward a chosen life change.

related.note: を境に stresses a before/after dividing line; を機に stresses seizing the event as an opportunity to act.

entry.title: 〜を限りに
entry.meaning: as of (the end of); ~ being the last
entry.summary: 〜を限りに takes a time point or occasion as the final cutoff, after which something stops or changes for good: 今日を限りに = as of today; 本日を限りに閉店 = closing as of today. The following clause typically states an ending — a retirement, a shop's last day, quitting a habit. (A separate fixed idiom 声を限りに / 力の限り means 'to the utmost' and is unrelated to this time-cutoff use.)
pitfalls: Marks a time point as the last one, after which something ends; the main clause is normally an ending or cessation.
Don't confuse it with the fixed phrase 声を限りに ('at the top of one's voice'), which is 'to the utmost', not a time cutoff.

examples.ja: 今シーズンを限りに、彼は現役を引退することを発表した。
examples.en: He announced that he would retire from active play as of the end of this season.
examples.f: ｜今[こん]シーズンを｜限[かぎ]りに、｜彼[かれ]は｜現役[げんえき]を｜引退[いんたい]することを｜発表[はっぴょう]した。

examples.ja: 本日を限りに、この店は五十年の歴史に幕を下ろす。
examples.en: As of today, this shop brings the curtain down on its fifty years of history.
examples.f: ｜本日[ほんじつ]を｜限[かぎ]りに、この｜店[みせ]は｜五[ご]｜十[じゅう]｜年[ねん]の｜歴史[れきし]に｜幕[まく]を｜下[お]ろす。

synonyms.note: をもって is a neutral formal 'as of / with (this)'; を限りに adds the feeling that this is the final time, the last.

related.note: を境に marks a dividing line with a before/after change; を限りに marks a final endpoint after which something simply stops.

entry.title: 〜をもって・〜をもちまして
entry.kana: をもって・をもちまして
entry.meaning: with; by means of; as of (a set time or point)
entry.summary: 〜をもって attaches to a noun in two formal senses. As 'by means of / with' it names the means, standard, or quality through which something is done — 誠意をもって対応する (deal with it in good faith), 書面をもって通知する (notify in writing). As 'as of / effective from' it marks a fixed point that draws a line — 本日をもって (as of today), 五時をもって (as of five o'clock) — after which a state ends or begins. をもちまして is the politer form heard in announcements and ceremonies. Both belong to written and formal spoken register, not casual で.
structure: Noun［point in time］＋をもって／をもちまして
pitfalls: Two distinct senses: 'by means of / with' (naming a method or quality) and 'as of / effective from' (a fixed cut-off point). Context tells them apart.
This is formal and written; in everyday speech で ('by means of') is normal, not をもって.
をもちまして is a politeness variant used in announcements, not a separate meaning.

examples.ja: 当店は本日をもちまして閉店させていただきます。
examples.en: As of today, our store will be closing for good.
examples.f: ｜当店[とうてん]は｜本日[ほんじつ]をもちまして｜閉店[へいてん]させていただきます。

examples.ja: 選考の結果は、後日書面をもってお知らせいたします。
examples.en: The results of the selection will be communicated to you in writing at a later date.
examples.f: ｜選考[せんこう]の｜結果[けっか]は、｜後日[ごじつ]｜書面[しょめん]をもってお｜知[し]らせいたします。

synonyms.note: にて is a formal で for means or place; をもって in its 'by means of' sense is even more formal and often names a quality or standard.

related.note: を限りに also sets a final cut-off point in time, but stresses that something ends there; をもって can mark either an ending or a starting boundary.

entry.title: 〜をよそに
entry.meaning: disregarding; ignoring; without regard to
entry.summary: 〜をよそに attaches to a noun — usually someone's worry, opposition, or concern — and says the subject went ahead as if it were none of their business. 親の心配をよそに (heedless of his parents' worry), 周囲の反対をよそに (ignoring everyone's objections). The nuance is often critical: the subject coolly brushes aside something they really ought to have taken into account. It is written and formal in flavor.
pitfalls: The ignored noun is typically other people's feelings, concern, or opposition, and the tone is frequently disapproving.
Do not confuse it with 〜をものともせず: をよそに coolly disregards what one should heed, while をものともせず bravely overcomes a hardship.

examples.ja: 親の心配をよそに、彼は危険な冒険の旅に出かけていった。
examples.en: Heedless of his parents' worry, he set off on a dangerous adventure.
examples.f: ｜親[おや]の｜心配[しんぱい]をよそに、｜彼[かれ]は｜危険[きけん]な｜冒険[ぼうけん]の｜旅[たび]に｜出[で]かけていった。

examples.ja: 住民の反対をよそに、工事は着々と進められた。
examples.en: Ignoring the residents' opposition, the construction pressed steadily ahead.
examples.f: ｜住民[じゅうみん]の｜反対[はんたい]をよそに、｜工事[こうじ]は｜着々[ちゃくちゃく]と｜進[すす]められた。

related.note: をものともせず admiringly overcomes a hardship; をよそに coolly, often selfishly, disregards concern one ought to weigh.
にもかかわらず neutrally says 'despite the fact that'; をよそに specifically shrugs off others' feelings or objections.

entry.title: 〜んがために
entry.meaning: in order to; for the sake of (literary)
entry.summary: 〜んがために is a literary equivalent of ために that expresses a strong, deliberate purpose — 'in order to ~'. It attaches to the same base as a verb's ない-form: 勝たんがために (in order to win), 生き延びんがために (in order to survive). The subject actively wants the goal, so the following clause states what was done to reach it. Modifying a noun it becomes んがための. This is bookish, formal language; ordinary speech uses ために.
structure: Verb［ない form, drop ない］＋んがために
Verb［ない form, drop ない］＋んがための＋Noun
pitfalls: する becomes せんがために, not しんがために.
There is no ない in the form: 行かんがために, not 行かないがために.
It is literary and written; in everyday speech use ために or ように.

examples.ja: 生き延びんがために、人々はあらゆる手段を講じた。
examples.en: In order to survive, people resorted to every means available.
examples.f: ｜生き延[いきの]びんがために、｜人々[ひとびと]はあらゆる｜手段[しゅだん]を｜講[こう]じた。

examples.ja: それは、真実を明らかにせんがための長い闘いであった。
examples.en: It was a long struggle waged in order to bring the truth to light.
examples.f: それは、｜真実[しんじつ]を｜明[あき]らかにせんがための｜長[なが]い｜闘[たたか]いであった。

synonyms.note: べく is likewise a literary 'in order to'; んがために foregrounds the subject's strong desire for the goal, while べく reads more as a stated objective.
ため(に) is the everyday 'in order to'; んがために is its bookish, emphatic counterpart.

entry.title: 上は
entry.meaning: now that; since (one has done)
entry.summary: 〜上は presents a decisive fact — usually a decision made or an action already taken — as grounds for the resolve or obligation that follows. 引き受けた上は = now that I've undertaken it. The second clause states determination or what must naturally be done. It is formal and somewhat literary; in everyday speech からには is more usual.
pitfalls: 上は is formal and follows a verb of decision or action already taken; the second clause expresses resolve or obligation.
In conversation, からには is the more natural choice.

examples.ja: 会社を辞めると決めた上は、迷わず前に進むだけだ。
examples.en: Now that I've decided to leave the company, all that's left is to move forward without hesitation.
examples.f: ｜会社[かいしゃ]を｜辞[や]めると｜決[き]めた｜上[うえ]は、｜迷[まよ]わず｜前[まえ]に｜進[すす]むだけだ。

examples.ja: 試合に出る上は、優勝を目指して全力を尽くすつもりだ。
examples.en: Since I'm taking part in the match, I intend to aim for victory and give it my all.
examples.f: ｜試合[しあい]に｜出[で]る｜上[うえ]は、｜優勝[ゆうしょう]を｜目指[めざ]して｜全力[ぜんりょく]を｜尽[つ]くすつもりだ。

synonyms.note: 以上は is very close in meaning; 上は is more literary and centers on a decision or action already taken.
からには is the everyday, conversational equivalent; 上は is more formal and written.

entry.title: ただ〜のみだ
entry.meaning: nothing but; merely; all that remains is
entry.summary: ただ〜のみだ frames something as 'nothing but ~' or 'all that is left is ~'. のみ is the literary equivalent of だけ, and ただ reinforces it with the sense of 'merely / simply'. あとはただ待つのみだ = all that remains now is to wait. It attaches to a dictionary-form verb or a noun and belongs to formal, written-style Japanese.
pitfalls: のみ is formal and written; in ordinary conversation だけ is the natural choice.
ただ here means 'merely / nothing but', not the unrelated ただ meaning 'free of charge'.

examples.ja: 準備はすべて整った。あとはただ本番を待つのみだ。
examples.en: All the preparations are complete. Now the only thing left is to wait for the real event.
examples.f: ｜準備[じゅんび]はすべて｜整[ととの]った。あとはただ｜本番[ほんばん]を｜待[ま]つのみだ。

examples.ja: 彼は弁明もせず、ただ黙ってうなずくのみだった。
examples.en: He offered no excuse and did nothing but nod silently.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]は｜弁明[べんめい]もせず、ただ｜黙[だま]ってうなずくのみだった。

synonyms.note: のみ alone already means 'only' in a literary register; ただ〜のみだ frames it emphatically as 'nothing but'.
だけ is the everyday word for 'only'; ただ〜のみだ is its formal, emphatic counterpart.

related.note: ばかり also limits to 'only / just', but colloquially and often with a nuance of excess; ただ〜のみだ is formal and clean.

entry.title: 〜だの〜だの
entry.meaning: and the like; ~ and ~ (dismissive listing)
entry.summary: Aだの Bだの lists representative examples, usually with a dismissive, complaining, or exasperated tone — 給料が安いだの休みがないだの = 'pay is low, there are no days off,' and so on. It attaches to nouns, plain-form verbs, and adjectives, and implies there are more grievances of the same kind. The listed items are often other people's complaints the speaker finds tiresome.
pitfalls: だの〜だの usually carries a dismissive or complaining nuance, unlike neutral とか〜とか.
The listed items are treated as a bothersome sample; the implication is that there are yet more of them.

examples.ja: 給料が安いだの残業が多いだの、彼は不満ばかり口にしている。
examples.en: The pay's low, there's too much overtime — he does nothing but voice complaints like these.
examples.f: ｜給料[きゅうりょう]が｜安[やす]いだの｜残業[ざんぎょう]が｜多[おお]いだの、｜彼[かれ]は｜不満[ふまん]ばかり｜口[くち]にしている。

examples.ja: 暑いだの寒いだのと、あの人はいつも文句が多い。
examples.en: Too hot, too cold — that person is always full of complaints.
examples.f: ｜暑[あつ]いだの｜寒[さむ]いだのと、あの｜人[ひと]はいつも｜文句[もんく]が｜多[おお]い。

synonyms.note: とか〜とか lists examples neutrally; だの〜だの adds a complaining, dismissive tone.
やら〜やら lists things amid confusion or overwhelm; だの〜だの leans toward criticism or grievance.

related.note: なり〜なり offers alternatives to choose from ('either ~ or ~'); だの〜だの merely lists grievances.

entry.title: 〜にかこつけて
entry.meaning: using ~ as a pretext; on the excuse of ~
entry.summary: 〜にかこつけて marks using something as a convenient pretext to do what one really wanted anyway — 'under the guise of ~, on the excuse of ~'. 出張にかこつけて = using a business trip as a pretext, 病気にかこつけて断る = beg off on the excuse of illness. It implies the stated reason is a cover for a hidden motive. It attaches to a noun and is somewhat formal.
pitfalls: It implies the stated reason is a pretext masking one's real aim, not a genuine cause.
It attaches to a noun; to build a pretext from a clause, nominalize first (〜のにかこつけて / 〜ことにかこつけて).

examples.ja: 彼は出張にかこつけて、地元の旧友と会っていたらしい。
examples.en: He apparently used the business trip as a pretext to meet up with old friends back home.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]は｜出張[しゅっちょう]にかこつけて、｜地元[じもと]の｜旧友[きゅうゆう]と｜会[あ]っていたらしい。

examples.ja: 体調が悪いのにかこつけて、気の進まない集まりを断った。
examples.en: On the excuse of feeling unwell, I turned down a gathering I wasn't keen on.
examples.f: ｜体調[たいちょう]が｜悪[わる]いのにかこつけて、｜気[き]の｜進[すす]まない｜集[あつ]まりを｜断[ことわ]った。

related.note: をいいことに exploits a genuinely favorable circumstance; にかこつけて uses something as a surface excuse to cover a real motive.

entry.title: 〜に言わせれば
entry.meaning: if you ask ~; in ~'s opinion (as they would put it)
entry.summary: 〜に言わせれば introduces a person's subjective, often assertive verdict on something — 'the way ~ sees it, if you ask ~'. 私に言わせれば = if you ask me, 専門家に言わせれば = as the experts would put it. It frames what follows as that person's opinion, frequently a pointed or critical one, rather than neutral fact. The person is marked with に.
pitfalls: It presents a subjective, often critical judgment, not objective fact; expect an opinionated statement to follow.
The holder of the opinion takes に: 私に言わせれば, not 私が言わせれば.

examples.ja: 私に言わせれば、彼のやり方は少し強引すぎる。
examples.en: If you ask me, his way of doing things is a bit too forceful.
examples.f: ｜私[わたし]に｜言[い]わせれば、｜彼[かれ]のやり｜方[かた]は｜少[すこ]し｜強引[ごういん]すぎる。

examples.ja: 専門家に言わせれば、この対策は場当たり的なものにすぎないそうだ。
examples.en: According to the experts, this measure is nothing more than a stopgap.
examples.f: ｜専門[せんもん]｜家[か]に｜言[い]わせれば、この｜対策[たいさく]は｜場当[ばあ]たり｜的[てき]なものにすぎないそうだ。

related.note: にしてみれば imagines how a situation feels from someone's standpoint; に言わせれば voices the opinion or verdict they would actually state.
にとって marks 'for ~ / to ~' as the one an evaluation matters to; に言わせれば introduces that person's own spoken judgment.

entry.title: 〜にかまけて
entry.meaning: being too absorbed in ~ (and neglecting other things)
entry.summary: 〜にかまけて marks being so preoccupied with one thing that other things get neglected — 'caught up in ~, too taken up with ~'. 仕事にかまけて家庭を顧みない = so absorbed in work that one neglects the family. It is inherently negative: the following clause states what was let slide. It attaches to a noun and belongs to a somewhat formal, self-reflective register.
pitfalls: It is always negative — being wrapped up in one thing causes neglect of another, named in the following clause.
It attaches to a noun (仕事にかまけて, 忙しさにかまけて), not directly to a plain verb.

examples.ja: 仕事にかまけて、家族との時間をずっとおろそかにしてきた。
examples.en: Absorbed in my work, I have long neglected time with my family.
examples.f: ｜仕事[しごと]にかまけて、｜家族[かぞく]との｜時間[じかん]をずっとおろそかにしてきた。

examples.ja: 日々の忙しさにかまけて、健康のことをすっかり忘れていた。
examples.en: Caught up in the busyness of daily life, I had completely forgotten about my health.
examples.f: ｜日々[ひび]の｜忙[いそが]しさにかまけて、｜健康[けんこう]のことをすっかり｜忘[わす]れていた。

related.note: にかこつけて uses something as a deliberate excuse; にかまけて is genuine over-absorption that causes unintended neglect.

entry.title: 〜甲斐もなく
entry.meaning: to no avail; in vain, despite one's efforts
entry.summary: 〜甲斐もなく says that despite the effort or care put in, it brought no worthwhile result — 'for all one's ~, it was in vain'. 看病の甲斐もなく = despite all the nursing, to no avail; 努力の甲斐もなく不合格だった = for all the effort, still failed. It attaches to a noun + の or a verb, and the following clause states the disappointing outcome. Its positive counterpart is 甲斐があって ('the effort paid off').
structure: Verb［plain form／た form］＋甲斐もなく
pitfalls: 甲斐もなく always leads to a disappointing result; if the effort paid off, use 甲斐があって instead.

examples.ja: 懸命な治療の甲斐もなく、祖父は静かに息を引き取った。
examples.en: Despite the devoted treatment, to no avail, my grandfather quietly passed away.
examples.f: ｜懸命[けんめい]な｜治療[ちりょう]の｜甲斐[かい]もなく、｜祖父[そふ]は｜静[しず]かに｜息[いき]を｜引き取[ひきと]った。

examples.ja: 必死に練習した甲斐もなく、本番では実力を出しきれなかった。
examples.en: For all my desperate practice, in vain, I couldn't show my full ability on the day.
examples.f: ｜必死[ひっし]に｜練習[れんしゅう]した｜甲斐[かい]もなく、｜本番[ほんばん]では｜実力[じつりょく]を｜出[だ]しきれなかった。
