antonyms.note: 〜甲斐がある means the effort was worthwhile and paid off; 甲斐もなく means it was all for nothing.

entry.title: 〜きっての
entry.meaning: the best/foremost ~ in (a group, place, or field)
entry.summary: 〜きっての singles someone or something out as the very best within a defined group, place, or field. The noun before きって names the domain, and the noun after is what ranks number one in it: この業界きっての実力者 = the leading figure in this industry, 当代きっての名優 = the finest actor of the age. It is a set adnominal form (きって + の + noun) with a somewhat elevated, admiring tone.
pitfalls: The first noun is the group or arena within which someone is foremost; the second is the one who ranks highest.
Fixed as きっての directly before a noun; it always modifies a following noun.
Used for a superlative standing ('the best in ~'), generally in a positive, admiring sense.

examples.ja: 彼女はこの業界きっての実力者として、広く名を知られている。
examples.en: She is widely known as the most capable figure in this industry.
examples.f: ｜彼女[かのじょ]はこの｜業界[ぎょうかい]きっての｜実力[じつりょく]｜者[しゃ]として、｜広[ひろ]く｜名[な]を｜知[し]られている。

examples.ja: あの古書店の主人は、町きっての物知りとして評判だ。
examples.en: The owner of that used-book shop has a reputation as the most knowledgeable person in town.
examples.f: あの｜古書[こしょ]｜店[てん]の｜主人[しゅじん]は、｜町[まち]きっての｜物知[ものし]りとして｜評判[ひょうばん]だ。

related.note: ならでは points to a quality only that person or place could produce; きっての ranks someone as number one within a group.

entry.title: 〜ずとも
entry.meaning: even without doing; even if not
entry.summary: 〜ずとも is a literary concessive: even without doing the verb, the main clause still holds. 言わずとも分かる = you needn't say it — I understand anyway. It is the classical equivalent of 〜なくても, built from the negative ず plus concessive とも, and する becomes せずとも. Today it appears in written style, formal speech, and set turns of phrase, lending a dignified or aphoristic ring.
pitfalls: It is literary register — in conversation, 〜なくても is the natural equivalent.
する becomes せずとも: 説明せずとも, not ×しずとも.
It attaches to verbs; for nouns and adjectives, use でなくとも or くとも patterns instead.

examples.ja: そこまで説明せずとも、この図を見れば誰でも理解できます。
examples.en: Even without explaining in that much detail, anyone can understand just by looking at this diagram.
examples.f: そこまで｜説明[せつめい]せずとも、この｜図[ず]を｜見[み]れば｜誰[だれ]でも｜理解[りかい]できます。

examples.ja: 実物を見ずとも、写真だけでその美しさは十分に伝わってくる。
examples.en: Even without seeing the real thing, the photographs alone fully convey its beauty.
examples.f: ｜実物[じつぶつ]を｜見[み]ずとも、｜写真[しゃしん]だけでその｜美[うつく]しさは｜十分[じゅうぶん]に｜伝[つた]わってくる。

synonyms.note: 〜なくても is the everyday equivalent; ずとも says the same in classical, written style.

related.note: までもない judges an action unnecessary ('no need to'); ずとも concedes its absence and moves on.
ことなしに states that something happens without the action; ずとも concedes 'even if it doesn't happen'.

entry.title: 〜とはいえ
entry.meaning: that said; even so; nonetheless
entry.summary: 〜とはいえ concedes a point and then states something that runs contrary to what that point would lead you to expect — 'even though ~, still ...'. It is more formal and written than とはいうものの, and can either join clauses or open a sentence as 'Nonetheless, ...'. 便利とはいえ、頼りすぎは良くない = convenient though it is, relying on it too much is bad. The main clause qualifies or resists the conceded premise.
pitfalls: More formal and written than とはいうものの; fine at the head of a sentence ('Nonetheless, ...').
The main clause presents something contrary to what the conceded part would suggest.

examples.ja: 規則とはいえ、これほど厳しいと従業員の不満も大きい。
examples.en: Rules or not, when they're this strict the employees' discontent runs high.
examples.f: ｜規則[きそく]とはいえ、これほど｜厳[きび]しいと｜従業[じゅうぎょう]｜員[いん]の｜不満[ふまん]も｜大[おお]きい。

examples.ja: 内定をもらった。とはいえ、入社までにはまだ準備すべきことが多い。
examples.en: I got a job offer. Even so, there's still a lot to prepare before I start.
examples.f: ｜内定[ないてい]をもらった。とはいえ、｜入社[にゅうしゃ]までにはまだ｜準備[じゅんび]すべきことが｜多[おお]い。

synonyms.note: とはいうものの is nearly identical in meaning, slightly softer and more conversational.

related.note: ものの concedes within a single sentence ('although'); とはいえ can stand alone as a sentence-opening 'nonetheless'.
ながらも concedes about one subject's own action or state ('even while ~ing'); とはいえ concedes a whole statement.

entry.title: 〜べくして
entry.meaning: as was bound to happen; inevitably
entry.summary: 〜べくして typically repeats the same verb — VるべくしてVた — to say that an outcome was bound to happen, the natural and inevitable result of the circumstances. 起こるべくして起こった事故 = an accident that was bound to happen. It frames the event as no accident of chance but the logical culmination of what came before.
structure: Verb［dictionary form］＋べくして＋Verb［same verb, た form］
pitfalls: It is almost always used with the same verb on both sides (勝つべくして勝った, 起こるべくして起こった).
It stresses inevitability given the conditions — the result was destined, not a coincidence.

examples.ja: 日頃の備えがあったからこそ、あのチームは勝つべくして勝ったのだ。
examples.en: It was precisely their everyday preparation that let that team win just as they were bound to.
examples.f: ｜日頃[ひごろ]の｜備[そな]えがあったからこそ、あのチームは｜勝[か]つべくして｜勝[か]ったのだ。

examples.ja: あれだけ無理を重ねれば、起こるべくして起こった不祥事と言えるだろう。
examples.en: With that much strain piled on, you could call it a scandal that was bound to happen.
examples.f: あれだけ｜無理[むり]を｜重[かさ]ねれば、｜起[お]こるべくして｜起[お]こった｜不祥事[ふしょうじ]と｜言[い]えるだろう。

related.note: べく uses the same root to express purpose ('in order to'); べくして expresses inevitability.

entry.title: 〜ぐるみ
entry.meaning: the whole ~; -wide; everyone/everything included
entry.summary: 〜ぐるみ is a suffix meaning 'the whole ~ together, involving everyone in it'. It attaches to a limited set of nouns: 家族ぐるみ (the whole family), 会社ぐるみ (company-wide), 町ぐるみ (the whole town), 地域ぐるみ, and 身ぐるみ (everything one owns). The image is of the named group acting or being involved as a single unit, with no member left out.
pitfalls: Attaches to a limited stock of nouns (家族, 会社, 町, 地域, 身); not freely productive.
Means 'the whole group as a unit', implying everyone in it is involved.
身ぐるみ is idiomatic for 'everything one has (on one)', as in 身ぐるみはがされる.

examples.ja: その不正は、一部の社員ではなく会社ぐるみで行われていた。
examples.en: The wrongdoing was carried out not by a handful of employees but by the entire company.
examples.f: その｜不正[ふせい]は、｜一部[いちぶ]の｜社員[しゃいん]ではなく｜会社[かいしゃ]ぐるみで｜行[おこな]われていた。

examples.ja: 隣の一家とは、もう何年も家族ぐるみの付き合いが続いている。
examples.en: We've kept up a whole-family friendship with the household next door for many years now.
examples.f: ｜隣[となり]の｜一家[いっか]とは、もう｜何[なん]｜年[ねん]も｜家族[かぞく]ぐるみの｜付き合[つきあ]いが｜続[つづ]いている。

entry.title: 〜にもほどがある
entry.meaning: there's a limit to; ~ goes too far
entry.summary: 〜にもほどがある is a sharp criticism that some behavior has crossed the bounds of what's acceptable — 冗談にもほどがある = there's a limit to joking, 失礼にもほどがある = that's rude beyond all limits. It attaches to a noun, adjective, or plain-form verb. The tone is emotional and reproachful, saying the person has gone well past a reasonable line.
structure: Verb［plain form］／い-adjective／な-adjective＋にもほどがある
pitfalls: It is a pointed rebuke that something is excessive, not a neutral statement that 'there is a limit'.
Common with 冗談・失礼・非常識・勝手 — nouns naming the excess being criticized.

examples.ja: 人の日記を勝手に読むなんて、失礼にもほどがある。
examples.en: Reading someone's diary without permission — there's a limit to how rude you can be.
examples.f: ｜人[ひと]の｜日記[にっき]を｜勝手[かって]に｜読[よ]むなんて、｜失礼[しつれい]にもほどがある。

examples.ja: いくら忙しいからって、何日も連絡しないなんて、ひどいにもほどがある。
examples.en: No matter how busy you are, going days without any contact is awful beyond all reason.
examples.f: いくら｜忙[いそが]しいからって、｜何[なん]｜日[にち]も｜連絡[れんらく]しないなんて、ひどいにもほどがある。

related.note: すぎる plainly marks 'too much'; にもほどがある adds indignation that a line of decency has been crossed.

entry.title: 〜をいいことに
entry.meaning: taking advantage of; exploiting (a favorable situation)
entry.summary: 〜をいいことに marks a favorable circumstance that someone exploits to do something they arguably shouldn't. It carries clear criticism: 親が留守なのをいいことに = taking advantage of the parents being out. A noun takes を directly; a clause is nominalized with の first (いないのをいいことに). The speaker disapproves of the person for seizing on the situation.
pitfalls: Almost always critical — the speaker blames someone for exploiting a situation, so it doesn't fit neutral 'given the chance' contexts.
After a clause, insert の before をいいことに: 先生がいないのをいいことに.

examples.ja: 彼は先生がいないのをいいことに、教室で騒ぎ始めた。
examples.en: Taking advantage of the teacher's absence, he started making a racket in the classroom.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]は｜先生[せんせい]がいないのをいいことに、｜教室[きょうしつ]で｜騒[さわ]ぎ｜始[はじ]めた。

examples.ja: 客が少ないのをいいことに、店員はずっとおしゃべりしていた。
examples.en: Taking advantage of there being few customers, the clerk chatted the entire time.
examples.f: ｜客[きゃく]が｜少[すく]ないのをいいことに、｜店員[てんいん]はずっとおしゃべりしていた。

related.note: をよそに means acting in disregard of others' concerns; をいいことに means actively exploiting a convenient situation for one's own ends.

entry.title: 〜に則って・〜に則り
entry.kana: にのっとって・にのっとり
entry.meaning: in accordance with (rules, tradition, procedure)
entry.summary: 〜に則って means acting in conformity with an established norm — a law, rule, tradition, format, or set procedure. 伝統に則って = in keeping with tradition, 手続きに則り = following the proper procedure. The 〜に則り form is the more written, formal variant. Use it when behavior is deliberately made to conform to a recognized standard or custom.
pitfalls: The object is a norm — a rule, law, tradition, or procedure — not a physical path or line (that role belongs to に沿って).
It is formal, ceremonial language; everyday speech would use 〜どおりに or 〜に従って.

examples.ja: 式は古くからのしきたりに則って執り行われた。
examples.en: The ceremony was conducted in accordance with age-old custom.
examples.f: ｜式[しき]は｜古[ふる]くからのしきたりに｜則[のっと]って｜執り行[とりおこな]われた。

examples.ja: 契約は法律に則り、正式な手続きを踏んで結ばれた。
examples.en: The contract was concluded in accordance with the law, following the proper procedures.
examples.f: ｜契約[けいやく]は｜法律[ほうりつ]に｜則[のっと]り、｜正式[せいしき]な｜手続[てつづ]きを｜踏[ふ]んで｜結[むす]ばれた。

synonyms.note: に基づいて means 'grounded on (a source)'; に則って means 'conforming to (a rule or tradition)'.
に沿って can follow a path, wish, or policy; に則って specifically conforms to formal rules or custom.

entry.title: かれ〜かれ
entry.meaning: whether ~ or ~; either way; to a greater or lesser degree
entry.summary: かれ〜かれ pairs two opposite adjective stems in a fixed idiom meaning that whichever of the two holds, the same conclusion applies. It survives only in set phrases: 遅かれ早かれ (sooner or later), 多かれ少なかれ (more or less, to some degree), 良かれ悪しかれ (for better or worse). The かれ is a classical adjective ending, so these are memorized wholes rather than a freely built pattern.
structure: い-adjective［classical stem］＋かれ＋（opposite）＋かれ［fixed set phrase］
pitfalls: Occurs only in fixed pairs (遅かれ早かれ, 多かれ少なかれ, 良かれ悪しかれ); not freely productive.
良かれ／悪しかれ use irregular classical forms from よし／あし, not the modern いい／悪い.
The point is that both alternatives lead to the same result, so it is not a real choice.

examples.ja: 遅かれ早かれ、隠していた事実はいずれ明るみに出るだろう。
examples.en: Sooner or later, the facts that were hidden will eventually come to light.
examples.f: ｜遅[おそ]かれ｜早[はや]かれ、｜隠[かく]していた｜事実[じじつ]はいずれ｜明[あか]るみに｜出[で]るだろう。

examples.ja: 人は誰でも、多かれ少なかれ何らかの欠点を抱えているものだ。
examples.en: Everyone, to a greater or lesser degree, carries some sort of flaw.
examples.f: ｜人[ひと]は｜誰[だれ]でも、｜多[おお]かれ｜少[すく]なかれ｜何[なん]らかの｜欠点[けってん]を｜抱[かか]えているものだ。

entry.title: とみえる・とみえて
entry.meaning: it seems that ~ (deduction from evidence)
entry.summary: 〜とみえる draws a conclusion from what you can observe: 'it seems that ~, judging by the evidence'. 〜とみえて connects that inference to a following clause that shows the evidence or result.
structure: Sentence［plain form］＋ とみえて ＋ Sentence
pitfalls: It's deductive — you infer a cause from a visible result — so it feels more reasoned than 〜そうだ ('looks like').
Somewhat literary; in everyday speech 〜らしい or 〜みたいだ are more natural.

examples.ja: 道が濡れている。夜に雨が降ったとみえる。
examples.en: The road is wet. It seems it rained during the night.
examples.f: ｜道[みち]が｜濡[ぬ]れている。｜夜[よる]に｜雨[あめ]が｜降[ふ]ったとみえる。

examples.ja: 疲れているとみえて、子どもはすぐに寝てしまった。
examples.en: The child must have been tired, since he fell asleep right away.
examples.f: ｜疲[つか]れているとみえて、｜子[こ]どもはすぐに｜寝[ね]てしまった。

synonyms.note: 〜らしい also infers from evidence but is more colloquial; 〜とみえる is more deductive and literary.

related.note: 〜そうだ reads an appearance directly; 〜とみえる reasons back to a cause.
〜ようだ is a broad 'it seems'; 〜とみえる specifically infers from observed evidence.

entry.title: 〜を踏まえて
entry.meaning: based on; taking ~ into account
entry.summary: 〜を踏まえて means taking established facts, results, or opinions as the grounds for the next judgment or action: 現状を踏まえて対策を立てる = draw up measures taking the current situation into account; 前回の反省を踏まえて = building on the lessons of last time. 踏まえる means 'to base oneself on', so the reference is something already known and considered, not a future hypothetical. It is formal and common in discussion and policy.
pitfalls: Take X (facts, results, opinions already established) as the basis for a judgment or action — not a future assumption (compare を前提に).
Formal register; typical objects are 現状・結果・意見・事実, things already on the table.

examples.ja: 前回の反省を踏まえて、今年は計画を大幅に見直した。
examples.en: Taking the lessons of last time into account, this year we substantially revised the plan.
examples.f: ｜前回[ぜんかい]の｜反省[はんせい]を｜踏[ふ]まえて、｜今年[ことし]は｜計画[けいかく]を｜大幅[おおはば]に｜見直[みなお]した。

examples.ja: 調査結果を踏まえて、今後の方針を決定する予定だ。
examples.en: We plan to decide our future policy on the basis of the survey results.
examples.f: ｜調査[ちょうさ]｜結果[けっか]を｜踏[ふ]まえて、｜今後[こんご]の｜方針[ほうしん]を｜決定[けってい]する｜予定[よてい]だ。

synonyms.note: をもとに uses X as source material to produce something; を踏まえて takes X into consideration as grounds for a judgment.

related.note: を前提に assumes a condition as given going forward; を踏まえて builds on facts already established.

entry.title: 〜ないとも限らない
entry.meaning: cannot rule out that ~; it's not impossible that ~ might happen
entry.summary: 〜ないとも限らない stacks two negatives (a negated predicate plus 〜とも限らない, 'it is not limited to') to make a cautious positive: 'one cannot say for certain that ~ won't happen', i.e. 'there is a chance it might'. 事故が起きないとも限らない = we can't rule out that an accident might occur. It typically raises the possibility of an undesirable outcome as a reason to stay careful, and belongs to formal or written registers.
structure: Verb［ない form］＋とも限らない
pitfalls: It is a double negative that lands on cautious possibility ('might well ~'), not a firm assertion; treat it as 'there's a chance', usually of something unwanted.
The ない belongs to the predicate you attach it to: 漏れない＋とも限らない, so the whole means 'it might leak', not 'it won't leak'.

examples.ja: 準備は万全だが、天候が急変しないとも限らない。
examples.en: Our preparations are thorough, but we can't rule out that the weather might suddenly turn.
examples.f: ｜準備[じゅんび]は｜万全[ばんぜん]だが、｜天候[てんこう]が｜急変[きゅうへん]しないとも｜限[かぎ]らない。

examples.ja: このデータが外部に漏れないとも限らないので、扱いには十分注意してほしい。
examples.en: There's no guarantee this data won't leak outside, so please handle it with the utmost care.
examples.f: このデータが｜外部[がいぶ]に｜漏[も]れないとも｜限[かぎ]らないので、｜扱[あつか]いには｜十分[じゅうぶん]｜注意[ちゅうい]してほしい。

synonyms.note: とは限らない plainly denies that something is always true; ないとも限らない adds a layer of negation to warn that the unwanted case might still occur.

related.note: ないでもない grudgingly admits 'it's kind of the case'; ないとも限らない instead flags a lingering possibility as a caution.
